how: The conformance work left a frozen inventory (docs/reconciliation/inventory-base.json) and a critique with a verdict for every module and command, and a test pins that coverage. That is a one-off record about the maintainers' process, not something sisi does or checks for later conformance work.
gap: No product mechanism: the test only checks that names from the inventory appear in critique.md, and cannot tell whether the current implementation was understood or used.
fix: Nothing checkable; a maintainer evaluation record exists, so only the process can carry it.

how: A SHOULD on how the reconciliation was carried out, not on the product. The verdicts on each existing component are a document (docs/reconciliation/critique.md); nothing in sisi can retain or improve components.
gap: Nothing is asked of the product; it is a process instruction to the people doing the conformance work.

how: A lead-in sentence ('The defining characteristics are:') that carries no requirement of its own; the seven characteristics that follow are graded as R-1-2 to R-1-8.
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: A unit must carry a non-empty goal (a placeholder goal is refused before any edit), and ending a reply on a question in prose instead of the question dialog is sent back once. Whether the goal is what the user actually needs is left to the agent.
gap: Nothing checks the goal against the user's request or keeps it current when the user amends the ask; accountability for the real need rests on rule 1 text.
fix: Needs the agent to compare the goal with the user's words; no code can check that.

how: Contract requirements carry a kind (explicit, implied, contextual, anticipated, experiential) and a decision (now, architect, defer, ignore). For integration and above, the gate and the before-tool hook refuse the work until a non-placeholder requirement list exists.
gap: Isolated and logic changes are asked for no requirement list, one entry of any kind satisfies the check, and nothing verifies that each kind was considered or that a deferred item is followed up.
fix: Require a requirement list at every profile and check each kind was considered.

how: A contract check that cannot fail is refused, checks carry a rung for the strength of their technique, and sisi verifiers ranks property, fuzz and proof techniques for a claim. Choosing them is the agent's decision; the gate only notes, never blocks, when no technique stronger than examples is used.
gap: Static analysis, strong types, mutation testing and formal methods are required by no profile; the technique note is one non-blocking line.
fix: Make the technique note blocking for logic and higher units lacking a rung-2 check.

how: Checks run only when a changed path matches (when_changed) and an identical tree reuses the last pass; a trivial change is asked for no contract, no checks and no retro; independent evidence is required only at data, critical and release.
gap: Time to first useful result and to validated completion is measured, not driven: nothing acts when a unit is slow, and the agent still decides which checks exist and how long they take.
fix: Acting on slow units is a process choice; no code can judge when delay is excessive.

how: sisi route picks the cheapest worker that the judged record or a benchmark says is capable (a property test over generated worlds). Parallelism is measured as overlapped delegations; coordination cost appears only as retries in the ledger.
gap: The router is advice the agent may override; parallel execution where it shortens the critical path, and the integration cost of delegating, are neither made nor checked.
fix: Parallelism and integration cost are judgement calls the router cannot enforce.

how: The unit scorecard records a lifecycle_quality dimension (files and lines changed, whether tests changed with code, whether the public surface was touched), and the done recipes say what makes refactoring and other kinds of work finished.
gap: Measured only: nothing in the gate or the hook refuses or flags a change that hurts reliability, clarity, maintainability or extensibility; those judgments are left to the agent and to recipe text.
fix: Lifetime quality of the result cannot be checked mechanically; only recorded.

how: When a unit's checks are green the gate offers the retro once per state of the tree, a generic finding is refused, a recorded finding closes the unit, and sisi cycle turns proposed learnings into enforced mechanisms, flagged when they recur twice.
gap: The offer is not repeated and a turn that ends without a retro is allowed, so units are not always evaluated; the cycle runs only when the agent acts on a session-start notice; a trivial unit gets no retro unless it shows an anomaly.
fix: Offer the retro on every unit and refuse turns ending without a retro or pause.

how: The scorecard keeps eight dimensions and no aggregate, and sisi status prints no score (a test asserts this). Activity counts such as lines, tokens and delegations are recorded only as diagnostics.
gap: The tests pin only the status text and the scorecard's keys. I did not confirm that no other reporter, rule or learning treats tests, coverage, agents or units closed as a target, and nothing detects such a target if one appears.
fix: No test can rule out gaming of targets in free text; only the scorecard keys are checkable.

how: A lead-in sentence ('The system's responsibilities include:') with no requirement of its own; the nine responsibilities that follow are graded as R-2.3-2 to R-2.3-10.
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: The desired outcome is held as the contract's goal, which must be non-empty (a placeholder is refused before any edit), and a reply that ends on a question in prose is sent back once so the question dialog is used.
gap: The goal is free text the agent writes: nothing compares it with the user's words, notices a changed request, or keeps a model of the outcome beyond that field.
fix: Whether the goal matches the user's outcome needs judgement, not code.

how: Each contract requirement has a kind (explicit, implied, contextual, anticipated, experiential) and a decision (now, architect, defer, ignore), validated by contract.validate; the gate demands the list from integration up.
gap: Below integration no list is asked; one entry of any kind passes; nothing checks that requirements are discovered, tracked to a check, or revisited when deferred.
fix: Require a requirement list at every profile, not only integration and above.

how: A contract has scope.in and scope.out and may carry a plan; for integration and above an approach (what was chosen, why, and a rejected alternative) is required before building.
gap: Scope and plan are optional and unchecked at every profile, the approach is asked only from integration up, and investigation and prioritization are entirely the agent's.
fix: Problem framing and prioritisation are judgement; only scope presence is checkable.

how: sisi does none of this work itself; the host agent does. The product adds the before-tool guard that refuses a non-trivial edit until a valid unit stands behind it, the recorded approach at integration and above, and the done recipes that say what makes each kind of work finished.
gap: No mechanism makes or checks architecture, design, refactoring, documentation or integration quality; the recipes are advice and the guard asks only for a contract.
fix: Architecture and design quality cannot be checked mechanically; recipes are advice.

how: sisi risk works out a floor from the changed paths (auth, secrets, crypto and installer paths are critical), and the gate demands what that profile's row requires: checks that can fail and say what they cover, invariants, a risk note and independent evidence. The verifier library lists safety techniques.
gap: No security analysis is performed; the test strategy is whatever checks the agent writes, and the floor is raised by the agent's judgment.
fix: Security analysis and test strategy quality need reviewer judgement, not a product check.

how: sisi route names the cheapest capable worker, a delegation naming no model or the session's own is refused with that pick, and the direct-work budget counts the main thread's calls. Task decomposition and parallel execution are left to the agent and only measured.
gap: Resource budgeting is a count of direct tool calls and result characters, not of money or time; decomposition and parallelism are neither made nor checked.
fix: Decomposition and parallel execution are agent decisions; only budgets are counted.

how: A retro finding promoted with a mechanism becomes, through sisi cycle, an enforced contract requirement, an enforced command check, a risk-table or routing adjustment, or a library entry in the user store; changes to sisi's own code go to the contribution export.
gap: This improves sisi's own organization, and only when the agent runs the cycle; nothing makes or checks improvements to the project's development workflow or infrastructure.
fix: Workflow improvement quality depends on the retro's findings, not checkable by code.

how: sisi handover lists learnings waiting to be filed in the project's docs, and a unit ends with one of five recorded delivery statuses. The delivery report itself is rule 7 text.
gap: Deployment, monitoring and recovery have no mechanism at all; the content and honesty of the delivery report are left to the agent, and handover covers filed learnings, not an operational handoff.
fix: Add deployment, monitoring and recovery records and checks for authorized releases.

how: Each closed unit gets telemetry and an eight-dimension scorecard with every value classed; the retro refuses generic findings and records learnings; sisi cycle promotes them into mechanisms and two recurrences flag one as not working.
gap: The retro is offered once and may be skipped, and the improvement step (the cycle) runs only when the agent acts on a notice; nothing shows the organization actually improved.
fix: Whether the organisation improved is a judgement over the record, not a code check.

how: The objective and its order are stated in the rulebook, and the scorecard records verified requirements, elapsed times, tokens and human attention as separate values so none stands in for another.
gap: Maximizing is the agent's behavior: sisi measures the terms and asks for evidence that fits the risk, but no mechanism acts on long-term value per unit of time, cost or attention.
fix: Maximising long-term value is an agent objective; no mechanism can measure it directly.

how: The learning loop exists: sisi retro records a finding with its cause, sisi cycle promotes proposed learnings into mechanisms, and a promoted learning that recurs twice is flagged so a cycle that ignores it is refused.
gap: The loop depends on the agent recording a retro and running the cycle when told; no measurement shows the objective being achieved better over time (trends say 'too few' under five units).
fix: Improvement over time needs a trend measure over many units, which cannot be built now.

how: The gate treats the profile's requirements as hard items: a failing check or a missing item sends the turn back whatever the speed or cost, and the only ways on are a recorded deviation or an unverified release.
gap: Below the gate, trading value against time, cost and attention is left to the agent; sisi holds the constraints but models no objectives.
fix: Trading objectives below the gate is judgement; the gate already holds the hard constraints.

how: A tier heading: it names a category and places no requirement until the sentences that follow (R-3.2-3 to R-3.2-6).
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: A project's contract commands run only after sisi contract trust on this machine; secrets are scrubbed from recorded findings; consequential learning changes wait for the owner's typed approval, and protected rules cannot be disabled.
gap: Legal and policy obligations are outside sisi; asking before a destructive, outward or costly action, least access for workers and treating tool output as data are rule 9 text left to the agent.
fix: Gate and checks can be switched off; add a required-on setting for security-critical paths.

how: A unit at integration or above must carry risk.rollback (how to undo it). sisi's own changes are recoverable: unit archives are never overwritten, and each cycle's change to the user store is committed and reverted exactly.
gap: For the project's own consequential changes recoverability is a written note, not a mechanism: nothing checks that a commit, backup or migration path exists before a hard-to-undo change runs.
fix: Check that a rollback note exists and a backup or commit reference precedes hard-to-undo changes.

how: sisi verify gives five statuses so nothing unrun reads as passed; unit close refuses 'delivered' while a check fails; a removed failing check stays in the record; a gate release is labelled unverified with the instruction to report it so.
gap: This keeps sisi's record honest; the agent's own report text and deployment status are not checked, and the gate can be switched off in config.
fix: Gate can be disabled; make honesty checks non-waivable and compare final report status with the record.

how: The send-back weighs no speed or cost argument, and after its send-backs run out the unit is released as unverified rather than complete; protected rules cannot be replaced or disabled by a cycle or by hand.
gap: Enforcement exists only where the end-of-turn hook is installed and enabled (gate.enabled can turn it off); a waiver lets a change without a contract end as a recorded deviation.
fix: Enforcement stops where the hook is absent or gate.enabled is false; make the gate mandatory.

how: A tier heading: it names a category and places no requirement until the sentences that follow (R-3.2-8, R-3.2-9).
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: The gate runs the contract's checks and sends the turn back on a failure; the profile's row of canon/risk.json sets the assurance threshold and each missing item is named; a failing check cannot close as delivered.
gap: The acceptance checks are written by the agent, not agreed with the user, and 'one check tests the purpose' is rule text; after three send-backs the turn ends with the criteria unmet (labelled unverified).
fix: Require the user to confirm acceptance checks at contract init before building.

how: A failing or blocking check sends the turn back, sisi unit close refuses to record the unit as delivered, and when the send-backs run out the gate releases the turn as unverified, never as complete.
A tier heading: it names a category and places no requirement until the sentence that follows (R-3.2-11).
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: The contract's goal and its requirement list (with implied and contextual kinds) are where the user's actual problem and its implied requirements are recorded, and the gate asks for that list from integration up.
gap: Preferring the better outcome among acceptable ones is the agent's judgment; sisi neither compares alternatives nor measures durable value beyond 'public surface touched'.
fix: Choosing the better outcome among acceptable ones is judgement; no code compares alternatives.

how: A tier heading: it names a category and places no requirement until the sentence that follows (R-3.2-13).
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: Checks are selected by change and reused on an identical tree, a trivial change is asked nothing, the router names the cheapest capable worker, and the direct-work budget refuses the main thread's calls past a limit.
gap: Minimizing time, cost, attention and future maintenance burden is measured, not enforced, apart from check selection and the call budget; the agent may do all the work itself with a stated reason.
fix: Trading time, cost and maintenance is judgement beyond the present check and call budgets.

how: A tier heading: it names a category and places no requirement until the sentence that follows (R-3.2-15).
gap: No requirement in this sentence.

how: Learnings from retros become, through sisi cycle, enforced requirements, checks, risk-table or routing adjustments, library entries and benchmark cases that later sessions receive; two recurrences flag one as not working.
gap: The cycle is due by a counter and announced, not run by sisi; whether judgment, quality, cost or latency improved is not shown (the learning report says 'too few' under five units).
fix: Whether later work got better judgement or lower cost is not checkable by code.

how: scorecard.py computes no aggregate: the unit record holds eight dimensions and sisi status prints trends per metric with no score, which a test asserts.
build_scorecard stores the eight dimensions separately, every value classed and missing data 'unavailable' rather than zero, and status prints each dimension.

The scorecard shows counters together (delivery time beside human corrections and requirements added late; tokens beside corrections), segments under five units say 'too few', and a promoted learning that recurs twice is flagged so a cycle that ignores it is refused.
gap: Nothing detects a metric being gamed or checks that a rule or learning targets one; the pairing exists only for the metrics the scorecard already has.
fix: Detecting a gamed metric needs judgement over behaviour; no code can flag it reliably.

how: Each dimension sits beside its counters in the same record, and sisi retro prints what stands out from the record (for example a check that failed then passed) as the qualitative evidence.
gap: A SHOULD, and only the built-in metrics are paired; a metric that becomes important later, such as one a rule or learning introduces, is paired by no mechanism.
fix: Lint that every newly added scorecard dimension names at least one counter-metric.

how: The only mechanism is the contract's goal: the before-tool guard refuses a non-trivial build while the goal is empty or a placeholder, and asks for 'the goal in the person's words'. Nothing can tell an outcome from a literal command; reading the request as an outcome rests on rule 1.
gap: Rests on the agent following rule 1 (canon/core.md:13). sisi checks only that some non-placeholder goal sentence exists, not that it names the outcome wanted.
fix: Telling an outcome from a literal command is interpretation; code can only check goal presence.

how: A contract requirement carries a kind that contract validation restricts to explicit, implied, contextual, anticipated and experiential, and the guard demands a requirement list before building at integration and above.
gap: No test feeds a requirement with a wrong kind, so deleting the kind check breaks nothing. One row marked explicit satisfies the gate, so no distinction among the five is ever demanded, and below integration no list is asked for.
fix: Add a test that a requirement with an invalid kind is refused.

how: 'explicit' is one of the five allowed values of a requirement's kind.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing requires that the user's stated requirements be listed as explicit, and no test uses any kind but explicit.
fix: Vocabulary definition of explicit requirements; places no testable product requirement.

how: 'implied' is one of the five allowed values of a requirement's kind.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing asks for implied requirements to be listed, and no test uses the value.
fix: Vocabulary definition of implied requirements; places no testable product requirement.

how: 'contextual' is one of the five allowed values of a requirement's kind.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing asks for codebase, convention or prior-decision requirements to be listed, and no test uses the value.
fix: Vocabulary definition of contextual requirements; places no testable product requirement.

how: 'anticipated' is one of the five allowed values of a requirement's kind.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing asks that foreseeable needs be recognised before they become defects, and no test uses the value.
fix: Vocabulary definition of anticipated requirements; places no testable product requirement.

how: 'experiential' is one of the five allowed values of a requirement's kind.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing asks for usability, polish or operational qualities to be listed, and no test uses the value.
fix: Vocabulary definition of experiential requirements; places no testable product requirement.

how: sisi contract init writes a contract with goal, scope, requirements, checks, invariants, assumptions, questions, deferred, limitations, plan and approach. A unit is demanded only for changes above the trivial profile, and only its goal and one real check are required.
gap: A trivial-profile request is asked for no model at all. Below integration the requirement list is not required, and assumptions, questions, scope and plan are never required at any profile.
fix: Require goal, requirement list and assumptions at every non-trivial profile, not only integration.

how: A unit cannot be built on until goal is a non-placeholder sentence; contract init takes it from --goal and the guard refuses the build otherwise.
gap: Only where a unit is required: a trivial-profile request records no goal. 'The problem being solved' is not asked for beyond the one goal sentence.
fix: Record the goal for every request above trivial and refuse a placeholder goal earlier.

how: At integration and above, the guard and the gate demand at least one requirement whose text is not a placeholder, and each entry must name one of the five kinds.
gap: Nothing requires an explicit entry: a list of only other kinds passes. Constraints have no field (scope is optional and unchecked), and below integration no requirements are asked for.
fix: Require at least one explicit-kind requirement entry before building.

how: No field of the contract records project or user context and no profile, guard or gate asks for it. sisi prompt injects matching lessons and a recipe as extra context for a request, but that is not part of the model and nothing records it.
gap: Nothing in the code puts relevant project or user context into the intent or requirement model.
fix: Add a project and user context field and have a gate ask for it.

how: 'implied' is an allowed requirement kind, validated by contract check.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing asks for implied requirements or for dependencies to be listed, and no test uses the value.
fix: Require a dependencies field and at least one implied entry for integration and above.

how: 'anticipated' is an allowed requirement kind, and deferred entries (what, why, safe_because) are validated and copied into the closed unit's record.
gap: Neither is required by any profile, edge cases and downstream needs are not asked for, and no test uses the 'anticipated' kind.
fix: Foreseeing edge cases and downstream needs is judgement a checklist can only prompt.

how: Every unit above the trivial profile needs at least one check that can fail (claim, command, expected exit) before the first build and again at the end of the turn; vacuous commands are refused.
gap: A trivial-profile request needs no check, so 'each meaningful request' is not covered: a meaningful documentation request records no acceptance criterion.
fix: Trivial profile needs no check by design; make that profile's exemption explicit and reviewable.

how: The contract has assumptions (a list of text) and questions (a question plus its default), and contract check validates their shape.
gap: No profile requires either, nothing asks for a confidence level, and a contract with both empty passes every gate.
fix: Require at least one assumption or an explicit none at non-trivial profiles.

how: The contract has scope.out, deferred (what, why and safe_because, each non-empty) and limitations; deferred entries are copied into the closed unit's record.
gap: All optional: no profile asks for them and empty lists pass. Nothing links a requirement decided 'defer' to a recorded follow-up.
fix: Require scope.out or a deferred entry linked to a follow-up record.

how: Only rule 1 asks the agent to work out what the request implies and to build what is obviously needed; the requirement list that comes out of it is demanded only at integration and above.
gap: Rests on the agent following rule 1: sisi neither infers requirements nor checks that an obvious, necessary one was implemented.
fix: Inferring obvious requirements is agent judgement; code cannot know what is obvious.

how: Every requirement entry must carry a decision of now, architect, defer or ignore; contract check rejects others, which blocks building. Rule 1 says not to expand the scope on speculation.
gap: No test gives a requirement a wrong decision, so removing the check breaks nothing. 'why' is optional, so a decision need not be justified, and below integration no entry is required.
fix: Add a test that a requirement with a wrong decision is refused.

how: The decision field forces one of the four choices on each requirement entry, at integration and above.
gap: Nothing asks for or weighs expected value or confidence, and no test covers the decision vocabulary.
fix: Weighing expected value and confidence is judgement; the decision field only records a choice.

how: 'now' is one of the allowed decisions.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing checks that a requirement decided 'now' was implemented, and no test would notice the value removed.
fix: Require every requirement decided now to name a check that covers it.

how: 'architect' is one of the allowed decisions.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing checks that room was actually left for the requirement, and no test uses the value.
fix: Whether room was left for a later need is a design judgement no code can verify.

how: A requirement can be decided 'defer', and deferred entries with what, why and safe_because are kept in the closed unit's record.
gap: Optional and unenforced: nothing requires a deferred item to be recorded, the two lists are not linked, and the follow-up is only stored; no mechanism communicates it to the user.
fix: Require each deferred entry to link to a follow-up record.

how: 'ignore' is one of the allowed decisions.
gap: Vocabulary only: nothing checks that what was ignored was speculative or low-value, and no test uses the value.
fix: Whether an ignored item was speculative or low-value is judgement, not checkable.

how: Rule 1 says find out before asking (canon/core.md:22). The one check is the question dialog refused once after a worker failure, with the fallback to use instead of asking the person.
gap: Only that one case is enforced. Whether any other question could have been inferred from context or discovered by investigation is never checked.
fix: Whether a question could have been inferred is judgement; only one case is checkable.

how: The contract has an assumptions list, and rule 1 tells the agent to record an assumption when a wrong guess is cheap to undo.
gap: Never required by any profile, guard or gate: recording assumptions rests on the agent following rule 1.
fix: Require the assumptions list to be non-empty at non-trivial profiles.

how: Only rule 1 asks the agent to ask when interpretations differ materially, the action is hard to undo, or the answer cannot be found (canon/core.md:23). sisi unit pause can record a wait on the person's authorization.
gap: No mechanism decides that a question or an authorization is needed, or refuses a consequential or irreversible action without one; it rests on the agent following rule 1.
fix: Deciding when clarification is needed is judgement; the pause record only stores a wait.

how: The end-of-turn gate sends back a reply that ends in a question asked in text instead of through the question dialog, and its message asks for options with the recommended one marked.
gap: Only the form is enforced, once per message, and only on hosts with a dialog. The number, specificity and relevance of questions are neither limited nor checked.
fix: Question count and relevance are judgement; the form is already enforced.

how: Rule 1 tells the agent to say when a better way would serve the goal and let the person decide (canon/core.md:25), and at integration and above the contract must record an approach with a rejected alternative.
gap: A permission the rulebook grants: nothing checks that a flawed request was challenged, and below integration not even an alternative is asked for.
fix: Challenging a flawed request is a judgement the person must be left to decide.

how: Before the first build at integration and above, the contract needs an approach with what was chosen, why, and at least one alternative; reuses can list existing capabilities.
gap: Only at integration and above. reuses is optional and unchecked, and unnecessary work, contradictory requirements and flawed premises have no field and are not asked for.
fix: Spotting flawed premises and unnecessary work is judgement no field can capture.

how: The goal is fixed in the contract before building and contract init refuses to replace an open unit. A later human message that reads as a correction is inferred from the transcript and counted in the unit record.
gap: Nothing compares the delivered work or the final report with the recorded goal, and the contract file can be edited freely. A correction is counted after the fact, never prevented.
fix: Detecting silent goal replacement needs judgement over the final report against the goal.

how: Several tested mechanisms keep 'passed' from meaning 'correct': a check that cannot fail is refused, the record has five statuses and never reports an unrun check as passed, invariants are required from integration up, and a logic-or-higher unit with only example tests gets a note. What is not enforced: nothing asks what correct behaviour means, the technique note never blocks, and invariants are not asked below integration.
gap: Choosing verification methods and stating what must stay true rest on the agent below the integration profile; the technique note is advice, not a check.
fix: Correctness as a property needs judgement about what must be true; checks prove only some of it.

how: The scorecard records intent fulfilment (requirements with a passing check) apart from correctness and assurance (results by status, techniques, checks seen failing, independent evidence). No code names or separates the five kinds of correctness of 5.1; integration and operational correctness have no field anywhere.
gap: Only two of the five kinds are told apart in the record; there is no distinction of integration or operational correctness, and nothing named for specification correctness.
fix: Add record fields for integration and operational correctness alongside the existing two.

how: A contract carries a requirement list (kind, text, decision, the check that covers it) that is validated and required from the integration profile up; the scorecard counts requirements with a passing check. Nothing checks that the requirements express the intended outcome; the spec-traceability and acceptance verifiers are catalogue text only.
gap: The requirement list is required only from integration up and is never compared with the intended outcome; whether the specification is right is left to the agent.
fix: Whether requirements express the intended outcome is judgement; no code can compare them.

how: Each unit's contract states claims as commands that can fail, the end-of-turn gate runs them against the code and is sent back while one fails (a check whose command cannot fail is refused).
gap: Overturned by the audit: Nothing in sisi distinguishes implementation correctness from the other four correctness kinds (grep finds no such term; check kinds are domain labels like money/parsing). Checks are only tied to requirements at integration level and above, so 'implementation satisfies the specification' is not separately established.

how: A change touching two or more top-level packages or a public interface is classed integration, which makes the gate require invariants (what must not get worse), a risk note and an approach. Nothing requires or records a check of the implementation against its surrounding components as such; invariants can be any command, and a single-package interface change is not raised.
gap: Integration correctness is not its own measured thing: no integration test is required and the record has no field for it.
fix: Require an integration check naming the surrounding components for cross-package changes.

how: The verifier library has real-world, concurrency and fault-injection entries that `sisi verifiers for` ranks for such requests, and a concurrency primitive in a path raises the floor to critical. No mechanism runs or requires a check under deployment, failure or load; that depends on the agent picking the entry.
gap: Operational correctness is catalogue advice only: no gate, profile requirement or record field covers deployment, failure or load.
fix: Add a deployment, failure or load check requirement and record its result.

how: Strength and independence are enforced and recorded: each check has a rung, the record notes whether it was ever seen failing, and independent evidence counts only when `by` names something other than the author (or an accepted review by another worker). The contract's `assumptions` list is only validated as strings: no profile requires it and it is not carried into the unit record or shown.
gap: Remaining assumptions are neither required nor reported; the proof boundary of a unit is not stated anywhere in its record.
fix: Carry the assumptions and proof boundary into the unit record and show them.

how: A verifier library in ten sections (prove, many-inputs, concurrency, real-world, test-quality, regression, safety, design, intent, completeness) covers the toolkit of 5.2, with a tested matcher that ranks entries for a claim and recipes per kind of work. Employing one is the agent's choice: the gate's pointer to the library is a note that never blocks.
gap: The toolkit is understood by the product, but its use rests on the agent following catalogue text; nothing records or requires that a technique was employed.
fix: Choosing and employing techniques is agent judgement; the library is advice.

how: The matcher scores entries by defect kind, section (system property), language, proven runs and rung, and the gate's note is keyed to the risk profile. The `cost` header is carried and printed but takes no part in ranking or in what the gate asks.
gap: Cost does not influence the choice, and risk only decides whether a non-blocking note is shown.
fix: Let the cost header weigh into the matcher ranking and the gate's note.

how: The library has property-testing entries for Python, Rust, Go, JavaScript/TypeScript and the JVM, the parser, money, feature and new-library recipes cite them, and the matcher puts a property or fuzz tool in the top three for parser and money claims. Parsing and algorithm paths are classed logic, but the gate only notes the absence of a rung 2 technique and does not name property testing.
gap: Favouring property tests is done by catalogue text and a non-blocking note; no logic change is required to have a property test.
fix: Require a property or fuzz check for logic changes with broad input spaces.

how: Six mutation-testing entries are in the library (three name equivalent mutants), recipes cite `mutation-on-diff`, and the record notes whether each check was ever seen failing. Nothing considers mutation testing for a unit unless the agent reads the recipe; the gate never asks for it.
gap: Mutation testing is advice only; the seen-failing flag is recorded but blocks nothing.
fix: Whether mutation testing suits a unit is a quality judgement the gate cannot make.

how: The library has a `prove` section (Lean, Dafny, Isabelle, CBMC, Kani, Z3, refinement types) and a `design` section (TLA+, Alloy, P, PlusCal, Quint), a rung 1 or 2 check satisfies `stronger_technique`, and the new-product recipe cites them. No profile requires a formal method for a critical invariant, a state transition or a data transformation; the critical profile asks only for independent evidence.
gap: Use of formal methods depends on the agent; the gate does not weigh assurance benefit against cost for critical, data or state-transition changes.
fix: Weighing formal-method cost against benefit is judgement; no code can make that call.

how: Proof boundaries are enforced for the library (every entry must carry a 'What a pass does not prove' heading, lint-checked; an entry written from memory is flagged) and the record reports every unrun check with its reason. The contract's `assumptions` list is optional, required by no profile and absent from the unit record.
gap: Assumptions of a unit are not reported: the field exists but nothing requires, carries or shows it.
fix: Require assumptions in the contract and report them in the unit record.

how: `sisi risk` works out a floor profile from the changed paths and diff keywords (what is touched, how many packages, whether auth, payments, migration or concurrency are in the blast radius), the contract declares a profile that may rise freely and lower only with a reason, and the gate and the before-tool guard require what that profile's row of canon/risk.json lists, including a blast-radius and rollback note from integration up.

A check with `when_changed` runs only when a changed path matches and is otherwise skipped with the reason recorded; identical inputs reuse the last pass; a trivial change needs no contract and the guard and gate ask nothing; every check runs only for a release.

`risk.classify_path` and `risk.assess` sort a change into one of seven profiles (trivial to release) from the file's kind, name and diff, checked against a set of independently labelled paths so that each gets its labelled floor.

The trivial profile is enforced as 'ask nothing': no contract, no refusal by the guard, a silent gate unless the unit shows an anomaly. Its row says 'the diff; a targeted check when one exists', but nothing acts on that text: `assure.missing` returns an empty list for trivial before looking at checks.
gap: Inspecting the diff and running a focused lint, snapshot or component check for a trivial change is not done or checked; the profile only removes ceremony.
fix: Run a focused lint or snapshot check for a trivial presentation change when one exists.

how: An isolated change must hold a contract with at least one check that can fail, and the gate runs it and sends back on failure. Nothing checks that the check is a unit or component test, a type check or a visual check; any non-vacuous command satisfies the profile.
gap: The kind of check is not distinguished: targeted tests, type checks and visual checks are not required or recorded.
fix: Record each check's kind and require one unit, type or visual check for isolated changes.

how: A logic change needs a contract whose every check says what failure it covers, and when no check is stronger than example tests the gate adds a note pointing at the library. Boundary and property tests, static checks and differential tests are named only in the recipes; the note never blocks.
gap: Only `covers` is enforced; property, differential and static checks for logic are advice a logic unit can pass without.
fix: Require at least one property, differential or static check for logic changes.

how: A change touching two or more top-level packages floors at the integration profile, whose row requires a contract whose checks each say what they cover, plus invariants (what must not get worse), a requirement list, a risk note and an approach; the gate and the before-build guard refuse until they exist. Nothing asks for affected-package, integration or compatibility checks as such.
gap: Only a generic contract is required (at least one check that can fail, each with covers, and invariants); affected-package tests, integration tests and compatibility checks are neither required nor selected by dependency, and the tests do not show that an integration change without them is refused.
fix: Require affected-package or integration checks when a change spans two or more packages.

how: Migration, schema and persistence paths floor at the data profile, which requires a rollback and blast-radius note, invariants, a requirement list, an approach and independent evidence; declaring a lower profile without a reason is refused by the gate.
gap: No migration validation, backward/forward compatibility or data-integrity check is required or run; rollback is a text field, not a rehearsed rollback or recovery check.
fix: Add migration validation, compatibility and rollback rehearsal checks for schema changes.

how: Authorization, secret, crypto, payment, concurrency-primitive, installer and hook paths floor at the critical profile, which requires invariants and independent evidence (an accepted judged review by another model, or a passing check marked independent and naming who produced it); the author's own model does not count.
gap: Nothing requires a threat-oriented review, adversarial cases, or race and state-space analysis; any accepted review with a check stronger than `none` satisfies the independent-evidence item whatever it looked at.
fix: Add threat-review and adversarial-case checks required for critical paths.

how: The release profile's row demands every check, deep ones included, fresh-passing on the tree before the gate lets the unit pass, and `sisi release` runs the source's own `sisi verify` and refuses when it fails.
gap: The release-profile branch that demands the deep checks be fresh has no test that would fail if it were removed, and `sisi release` runs the slow tier only when `--deep` is passed, so broader regression is not required by default.
fix: Add a test that removing the release branch's fresh-deep-check demand fails.

how: The risk floor is computed from the paths actually changed and the diff text, with a structural rule for several top-level packages and dependency files (lockfile, manifest, vendored code) floored at integration; checks select themselves against the changed paths.
gap: sisi does not follow actual code dependencies (who imports or calls the changed module) to find what the change affects; selection rests on when_changed globs the agent writes by hand, and nothing requires them.
fix: Compute the code dependency graph to find what a change affects.

how: Verification time is cut automatically: a trivial change runs nothing, slow checks sit in a deep tier that never runs at the end of a turn, the gate has a time budget, and a pass on identical inputs is reused; durations and the time saved are recorded, and the profile's requirements still hold.
gap: Only time is measured; the cost of a check is never estimated or bounded, and holding back checks that are irrelevant to the change depends on the agent having written when_changed.
fix: Bounding the cost of checks is judgement beyond recording time; cost is not estimated.

how: The lower bound is enforced (each profile demands a minimum of checks, covers, invariants and evidence) and a check whose when_changed matches nothing in the change is skipped with the reason recorded.
gap: Nothing stops or flags excess verification: a check without when_changed runs on every change at every turn, and no command reports that a unit runs more than the change needs.
fix: Flag checks that run on every change lacking when_changed, with a recorded reason.

how: An expensive check is one in the deep tier: a fast check whose timeout exceeds the fast limit is refused as invalid, and `sisi verify` lists the slowest checks by measured duration.
gap: The tier rule has no test of its own, and of the six things the lead asks the planner to identify for an expensive check only the failure it covers and reuse from a prior run are enforced; the rest are optional or absent.
fix: Add a test for the deep-tier rule that refuses a fast check with a long timeout.

how: Every check in a logic-or-higher unit must carry `covers` (the failure that check would catch); placeholder text counts as missing, the gate and the before-build guard name the check, and the value is stored with every result.
A check's `when_changed` path patterns name the components that make it relevant, are validated, and drive selection: no changed path matching means the check is skipped with that reason recorded.
gap: The field is optional: no profile asks for it, so for an expensive check written without it sisi cannot say which components make it relevant and the check runs on every change.
fix: Require when_changed on deep-tier checks at contract validation.

how: Every check and invariant must carry a non-empty `claim` (what the check shows to be true) to pass `sisi contract check`, and a failed run stores the lines that identify the failure as its evidence.
gap: No test removes the claim and expects a refusal, so nothing would catch the requirement disappearing; and only emptiness is refused, so a placeholder claim such as `TODO` is accepted outside the untouched skeleton.
fix: Add a test that a contract check without a claim is refused.

how: Every result stores its measured duration, the last duration of each check is kept and used as the estimate of time saved by a skip or reuse, and `sisi verify` prints the slowest checks and the time saved.
gap: Duration is known only after a check has run once; nothing reports an estimate for a check that has not run, and resource cost (processor, memory, tokens) is never estimated or recorded.
fix: Report an estimated duration for checks that have not yet run.

how: `sisi verifiers for "<claim>"` ranks the library's checks for a claim by relevance, rung, cost and whether the tool is installed, so a cheaper or more targeted check for the same claim can be found.
gap: It is a library lookup keyed by text the agent types, not by the contract's checks: no command takes an expensive check and says whether an equivalent or more targeted one exists, and nothing prompts the agent to look.
fix: Finding an equivalent or cheaper check is judgement; the library lookup can only prompt it.

how: A prior pass is reused only when the check's command, expectation and inputs (the files its when_changed watches, or the whole tree) hash identically; the result is then recorded as skipped with the time of the reused pass, never as passed, a failure is never cached, and `--all` disables reuse.
A check with when_changed that no changed path matches is recorded as skipped (not affected by this change) with that reason stored, and a skipped result never blocks delivery or the unit's close.
gap: Only a check that declares when_changed can be held back; a check with no stated connection to the change runs every time and blocks on failure, and no justification is asked for or recorded.
fix: Require a recorded justification for a check with no when_changed connection.

how: Every closed unit must record at least one retro finding, and a finding may be promoted as a mechanism of type verification or infrastructure, validated by replay before it is enforced.
gap: Nothing steers findings toward verification infrastructure, measures whether the infrastructure got better, or treats it as a preferred investment; it improves only when the agent chooses that disposition.
fix: Investing in verification infrastructure is a priority choice no code can enforce.

how: Every run appends one stored row per check result (contract, project, status, reason, duration, evidence), and closing the unit archives every verification result plus the latest state of each check in the unit record.

Exactly five statuses exist (passed, failed, skipped, not-applicable, not-run); each of the last three carries a reason, a timeout is not-run and a watch that matches no file is not-applicable, and the table, the stored rows and the gate all keep them apart.

A check that did not run is never stored, printed or counted as passed (the text says `did not run (not a pass)` and `no evidence yet`), a mandatory check that never passed stops a plain close, a check that cannot fail is refused, and the gate notes once when no check is stronger than example tests.

The meter refuses direct tool calls past a per-turn budget and makes the agent delegate or record a reason; the gate lets a turn end as soon as the selected checks pass and records timings. Nothing checks that time from intent to delivery is being minimised; that rests on rule 5.
gap: No mechanism measures or acts on intent-to-delivery time as a target; only the direct-work budget nudges it.
fix: Minimising intent-to-delivery time is a goal; only the direct-work budget acts on it.

how: unit.build_telemetry records time to first useful result and time to validated completion, each with a class, when a unit closes.
gap: Both measures are proxies with gaps of their own (see R-6.1-3, R-6.1-4); the test checks only the value's class.
fix: Add a test that telemetry records both measures with their values, not only classes.

how: The gate writes a delivery row at every stop it allows, with seconds from the last message the human typed; unit telemetry takes the first such row in the unit's window as the measured value, else infers it from the first green run.
gap: Any allowed stop counts, including one with no contract or one released as unverified, so 'useful' is not established; no test feeds delivery rows into the unit telemetry (only the inferred fallback is tested).
fix: Count only useful increments as first results; exclude unverified releases from delivery rows.

how: At sisi unit close, time_to_validated_completion_s is close time minus the unit's start, and a unit with a blocking check cannot close as delivered.
gap: The start is the unit's start (contract init or file mtime), not the user's request; the end is the moment the agent runs close, not the moment the outcome met acceptance; the test asserts only the class.
fix: Measure from the user's request time and record when acceptance was actually met.

how: Telemetry records time in checks, time in waits (pauses), time in delegations and send-backs per unit.
gap: Queue time, active execution time and integration time are not measured; waiting on tools is only partly covered by pauses.
fix: Add queue, active and integration time fields to unit telemetry.

how: The gate releases the turn as soon as the selected fast checks pass and records a delivery; sisi unit pause lets a unit wait without demands.
gap: Nothing checks that a meaningful increment is delivered as soon as it is useful; that is left to the agent following rule 5.
fix: Deciding when an increment is useful and validated is judgement, not checkable.

how: Checks with when_changed run only when the change touches a watched path; others are skipped with the reason recorded, and deep checks never run in the end-of-turn gate.
gap: Checks without when_changed always run, and nothing addresses work held for unrelated investigations.
fix: Holding work for unrelated investigation is a judgement; code cannot see the intent.

how: decide_status refuses 'delivered' when a check blocks or a mandatory check never ran (the unit becomes delivered-with-deferred, deviation, unverified or abandoned), and close_unit refuses to close a blocked unit.
gap: I found no code in assure.py, unit.py or gate.py that enforces the release profile's every-check requirement at close, so the 'bypass release requirements' part is not confirmed.
fix: Enforce the release profile's every-check requirement at unit close.

how: The meter refuses the fourth identical failing shell command when no file changed, and refuses calls past the per-turn call or character budget; checks have timeouts and durations are recorded.
gap: Nothing watches for stalled agents or delegations that never return, nor for unnecessary approval waits; low-value verification is only visible as check durations.
fix: Watch for stalled delegations and unnecessary approval waits, with alerts.

how: Each check runs under a timeout and the gate's run under a deadline; a check over the budget is reported not-run. The meter is a per-turn budget on direct calls.
gap: Budgets exist for checks and direct tool calls only; delegations and investigations have no time budget or progress checkpoint in code.
fix: Give delegations and investigations time budgets with progress checkpoints.

how: A repeated failing command is refused once with a message telling the agent to diagnose or change the approach; a specific reason is required to extend the direct-work budget.
gap: The refusal is a message; whether the agent reassesses is not checked, and the same command is let through after the one refusal.
fix: Whether the agent reassessed its approach is judgement; a refusal can only prompt it.

how: The budget refusal names the router's pick for reading and for building, and two ways on: delegate with a brief, or record why direct work is cheaper.
gap: Changing strategy, narrowing, parallelising or asking is advice in a refusal message; nothing verifies any of them happened.
fix: Changing strategy or asking is judgement; no code verifies the agent did either.

how: Send-backs are bounded (after three the unit is released as unverified and recorded), and the fourth identical failing command is refused once.
gap: The repeat refusal is once only (the test asserts the next run goes through) and the call budget restarts each turn, so an agent can still persist indefinitely across turns.
fix: Keep the repeated-failure refusal in force across turns, not once only.

how: verify.run defaults to the fast tier, runs a when_changed check only when the change touches a watched path, and runs everything only with --all.

verify.run selects checks from the paths changed since the unit started (change impact), and the gate asks the risk profile's requirements through assure.requirements and assure.missing (risk-adaptive).
Checks carry a mandatory flag (optional ones may be kept back at close) and every skip or reuse stores its reason; durations are recorded and the slowest checks printed.
gap: No field records why a suite is expensive (only its tier and measured duration).
fix: Add a field recording why an expensive suite is expensive.

how: With parallel true in the contract, fast checks run in a thread pool of at most four; a check marked serial runs alone so results match the serial run.
gap: Overturned by the audit: Concurrency exists only as an opt-in contract flag `parallel`; nothing sets it, recommends it or judges independence or contention, so sisi does not make concurrent runs happen. The cited test shows the pool works when flagged, not that it is used where it helps.

how: sisi status reports median and p95 of completion and first-result time per project, risk profile, model and policy version.
gap: These are baselines only: there are no target budgets and nothing is broken down by task class.
fix: Setting latency targets by task class needs data and judgement, not a single code change.

how: scorecard.trends computes the median (p50) and p95 of six time and size metrics per segment, and refuses a percentile from fewer than five units.
A unit is bound to the main session, subagent stops never satisfy the gate, and the gate sends the main thread back until it has judged every finished delegation.
gap: Accountability is enforced only as 'judge your workers' and 'your own edits are gated'; intent, prioritisation and architecture remain the agent's unaided responsibility.
fix: Owning intent and architecture is the main agent's judgement; the gate covers delegation only.

how: The gate asks once per set of finished unjudged runs for a judgement with the check applied; integration-and-higher units need an approach, invariants and independent evidence.
gap: Nothing checks that conflicting findings were reconciled or that integration quality was reviewed beyond the recorded judgement.
fix: Reconciling findings and reviewing integration quality is judgement beyond the recorded review.

how: routing.choose picks from the judged record by task kind and difficulty, benchmark standing, accepted rate, price and load.
gap: Latency and context needs are not inputs to the choice (routing.py has no notion of either).
fix: Add latency and context-window requirements as inputs to routing.choose.

how: routing.choose takes the cheapest of the capable workers, and the before-tool guard refuses a delegation that names no model or the session's own model, giving the router's pick.
Capability is assessed from the ledger of judgements (sisi delegate judge), prices and benchmarks are stored facts with a source and date, and the pick changes as the record changes.
Tokens by category and model come from the transcript, cost is estimated from recorded price facts, retries are send-backs, and the meter counts tool calls and result characters.
gap: External services, infrastructure and abandoned work are not costed; cost is unavailable when a model has no recorded price.
fix: Cost external services, infrastructure and abandoned work from recorded inputs.

how: I looked for a cost per accepted change or per unit of verified value and found none; the only related figure is an evaluation run's cost cap.
gap: No measure of cost per accepted change or per unit of verified user value exists.
fix: Compute cost per accepted change from the unit record and show it in status.

how: The meter never counts sisi commands such as verify, so saving calls cannot cut verification, and judgement work may continue with a recorded specific reason.
gap: Nothing checks that a saving in tokens or calls cost correctness; that trade-off rests on the rulebook.
fix: Trading token savings against correctness is judgement the rulebook states; no code can weigh it.

how: The budget pushes work to workers, and the scorecard records how many delegations overlapped, worker minutes against wall time.
gap: Parallelism is measured, not made to happen, and no comparison of wall-clock saved against added cost exists.
fix: Deciding whether parallel work pays is judgement; only overlap is measured.

how: The brief template has a required 'Files you may change' part and a 'Budget and escalation' part for dependencies; delegate check reports the parts a brief lacks.
gap: Nothing checks that two live delegations share files or depend on each other.
fix: Refuse concurrent delegations whose brief file lists overlap.

how: sisi delegate --brief refuses a brief without outcome, acceptance or the files the worker may change; delegate check names every missing part.
gap: Enforced only on the sisi delegate path; a host's own delegation tool gets advice text, and integration points are not a brief part.
fix: Enforced only on sisi delegate; host delegation tools get advice text only.

how: The scorecard records overlapped delegations and worker minutes against wall time, but I found no code that compares the wall-clock time saved by parallel work with the extra compute or coordination it cost.
gap: No measure of wall-clock reduction against added compute and coordination cost.
fix: Report wall-clock saved against worker minutes and coordination cost per unit.

how: The brief template has eight parts covering the list, and delegate check reports each part a brief lacks.
gap: Only three of the eight parts are required before sisi delegate runs a brief; the others are template and report only.
fix: Require all eight brief parts before sisi delegate runs a brief.

how: Outcome and scope is a required part: delegate check exits non-zero naming it when absent or a placeholder, and sisi delegate will not run the brief.
gap: Overturned by the audit: Refusal of a thin brief applies only to `sisi delegate`; native host delegations get only non-blocking post-hoc advice (orchestration.py:731). The cited test covers only `delegate check` output, and 'bounded' scope is never judged, only non-placeholder text.

how: The template has a 'Context and sources of truth' part and delegate check reports it when missing.
gap: Not required: a brief without it still runs.
fix: Require the context and sources-of-truth part before a brief runs.

how: Acceptance is required (sisi delegate refuses without it); constraints and interfaces is a separate, optional part.
gap: Constraints and interfaces are only reported, never required.
fix: Require constraints and interfaces before a brief runs.

how: The template has a 'Deliverables and report format' part and delegate check reports it when missing.
gap: Not required: a brief without it still runs.
fix: Require the deliverables and report format part before a brief runs.

how: Files the worker may change is a required part: delegate check exits non-zero naming it when absent, and sisi delegate will not run the brief.
gap: Overturned by the audit: Same gap: the 'Files you may change' requirement is enforced only for `sisi delegate`; a native Agent delegation is only advised afterward. The cited test checks `delegate check` output, not a refusal, and does not check that the listed files are actually bounded.

how: The template has a 'Verification' part and delegate check reports it when missing.
gap: Not required: a brief without it still runs.
fix: Require the verification part before a brief runs.

how: The template's 'Budget and escalation' part asks for a time or cost budget, and delegate check reports the part when missing.
gap: Not required, and no budget given to a worker is tracked or enforced.
fix: Require a time or cost budget before a brief runs, and track it.

how: Escalation shares the 'Budget and escalation' part of the template; delegate check reports the part when missing.
gap: Not required; dependencies are not named in the part and nothing checks them.
fix: Require the escalation and dependencies part before a brief runs.

how: brief.advice flags a vague acceptance, a gate with no abuse cases, tests with no repeat run and similar, and the router is asked for a kind and difficulty before the first delegation.
gap: Advice only: a broad, ambiguous brief is never refused on a host's delegation tool.
fix: Avoiding broad assignments is judgement; a host's tool cannot be refused on vagueness.

how: The meter refuses direct calls once a turn's results pass a character budget or its calls pass a count, repeated failing commands are refused once, and injected prompt context is capped at 2,000 characters.
gap: Duplicate analysis and unnecessary handoffs are neither measured nor refused; the budget restarts every turn.
fix: Avoiding duplicate discovery is judgement; duplication is not measured across handoffs.

how: The only mechanism that looks past the immediate task is the contract's requirement list (kinds include anticipated, contextual, experiential), which the end-of-turn gate demands for integration-and-above units. Nothing in the code asks about maintainability, reliability, security, performance, scalability, accessibility, observability or change cost, and below integration nothing is asked.
gap: A requirement list is enforced only at integration and above; the quality concerns the text names have no mechanism, check or measurement and rest on the agent's own judgement.
fix: Optimising beyond the task is judgement; quality concerns have no measurable check.

how: Searched sisi/ and canon/ for complexity, simplicity and accidental: no mechanism measures, asks about or records accidental complexity. The enforced approach note (chosen, why, alternative) records a design choice but says nothing about complexity, and the rulebook carries no advice on it.
gap: Nothing in the code does it; not even a recorded field or a retro question addresses accidental complexity.
fix: Accidental complexity cannot be measured by code; only a recorded reflection is possible.

how: No code counts lines, files or abstractions as a goal or a score; lines_changed is telemetry only. Nothing checks or prevents the organization from equating simplicity with the fewest lines, and the rulebook does not mention it.
gap: No mechanism detects or refuses the prohibited behaviour; the prohibition exists only in the specification.
fix: Distinguishing simplicity from fewest lines is judgement; code cannot detect the equation.

how: Searched sisi/ for architecture and consistency: nothing. Invariants protect behaviour, not structure; the contract's optional approach.reuses key is validated for shape only and nothing asks for or reads it.
gap: No mechanism asks whether a change keeps the existing architecture, conventions or patterns.
fix: Architectural consistency is judgement; no code can reliably check it.

how: A MAY: a permission to challenge architecture, not an obligation. Nothing in sisi prevents it, and the enforced approach note (chosen, why, alternatives rejected) is where such a challenge would be recorded.
gap: The text places no requirement on the product.

how: A unit's deferred items (what, why, safe_because, validated), limitations and open risks are archived in the record, and a unit with a deferred or never-run mandatory check cannot close as plainly delivered.
gap: Limitations and open risks are recorded only when the agent volunteers them (open_risks is not validated and no gate asks for it); nothing carries debt forward between units or reports it as debt.
fix: Carry open risks and limitations forward between units and report them as debt.

how: The approach note (what was chosen, why, an alternative rejected) is validated, archived in the record, and the end-of-turn gate demands it for integration-and-above units.
gap: The approach has no field for expected revisit conditions (keys are chosen, why, alternatives, reuses); nothing distinguishes a deliberate tradeoff from deterioration; below integration nothing is asked. The before-tool guard is written to refuse the build without it, but its test failed when I ran it (the edit was let through).
fix: Add a revisit-conditions field and fix the before-tool guard that let an approach-less edit through.

how: Two of the concerns are enforced: the risk note (blast_radius and rollback) is demanded for integration-and-above units, and deployment and release paths raise the risk floor to the release profile, whose row requires every check.
gap: Monitoring, alerts, incident diagnosis, data recovery, performance and operational handoff have no mechanism; only rollback and deployment risk are asked for.
fix: Add monitoring, alerts, incident and recovery records to delivery gates.

how: The before-tool guard refuses a non-trivial build without a valid unit, the end-of-turn gate sends the turn back until the unit's checks pass and a retro or a pause is recorded, and a trivial change is asked nothing.
gap: Only the contract, verification and retro stages are enforced. Discovery, planning, prompt reporting and the second retrospective have no mechanism, so an agent can skip them and nothing records it.
fix: Add discovery and planning stages to the lifecycle, enforced and recorded.

how: The direct-work budget refuses a main thread's tool calls past the limit and names the router's pick for reading and searching; rule 6 and the playbook say to run independent work in parallel and to delegate reading and research.
gap: Nothing asks for research to be split into independent questions or run in parallel. The budget only moves legwork off the main thread, and a recorded reason extends it.
fix: Splitting research into parallel questions is judgement; the budget only moves legwork.

how: I looked for anything that asks for, rewards or limits broad repository analysis and found none: no rule sentence, contract field, gate or refusal addresses targeted evidence gathering.
gap: Nothing in the code prefers targeted evidence gathering over broad, expensive analysis.
fix: Preferring targeted evidence over broad analysis is judgement; code cannot judge breadth.

how: At integration and above the contract must carry invariants (what must not get worse) and a risk note (what this can break, how to undo it); approach.reuses can name existing capabilities.
gap: Only at integration and above. reuses and technical debt are never asked for, and nothing checks that this happened before a new mechanism was proposed.
fix: Identifying existing functionality before new mechanisms is judgement; the reuses field is optional.

how: Ceremony follows the risk profile in canon/risk.json: a trivial change needs no contract and each higher profile asks for more, so a small task is not made to plan heavily.
gap: 'Sufficient to avoid foreseeable rework' has no mechanism: plan is an optional, unchecked list, and nothing asks for dependencies, parallelizable tasks or integration points.
fix: Planning sufficiency is judgement; no code can tell foreseeable rework was avoided.

how: Nothing asks a worker to report a discovery that changes scope, risk, architecture or estimates, and nothing checks that one arrived. The nearest thing is the brief template's optional 'Budget and escalation' line.
gap: No mechanism, rule sentence or record covers prompt reporting of discoveries by agents.
fix: Add a worker report channel for discoveries that change scope, risk or estimates.

how: A worker's stop is never evidence: decide_subagent only records what the worker edited, those edits count as the main session's, so the main session's gate runs the unit's checks on the integrated tree and sends it back on failure. Finished delegations are sent back once per set until the main session judges each (sisi/orchestration.py:993, tests/test_meter.py::test_the_gate_asks_for_the_judgements_once_per_set_of_runs).

When a worker failure was recorded this turn, the gate sends back once a final message that names the unavailable worker, provider or failure, and tells the agent to report only what the person receives.
gap: Only that one case is checked, once, on the recorded names. Every other orchestration detail in a report rests on rule 7.
fix: Keeping orchestration detail out of reports is judgement beyond the single gate check.

how: The contract records a parent request id and the closed record keeps it, but nothing groups units by it or asks for a cross-unit retrospective. The retro is per unit and the learning cycle is started by a counter.
gap: No second retrospective at the end of a multi-unit request, and no rule sentence asks for one.
fix: Group units by parent request and require a cross-unit retro at the end.

how: Searched sisi/ for anything on unit size or fragmentation: no mechanism measures how large a unit is, how many units a request was split into, or the coordination they caused. Refusing a second contract while one is open bounds the count of open units, not their size.
gap: Nothing in the code steers between oversized and fragmented units.
fix: Choosing unit size and granularity is judgement; no code can measure the right size.

how: sisi unit close archives the whole record to .sisi/units/<id>.json (written whole or not at all, never replaced) and appends a summary line to the user store; the gate closes the unit itself once a retro is recorded.
gap: A trivial-profile change needs no contract and is asked nothing, so it ends with no record of any kind, although the specification's own example of a very small work unit (a styling change, with telemetry) says otherwise; the record also exists only once the unit is closed.
fix: Write a minimal durable record for trivial changes too.

how: fresh_id gives a unit an id no archived, summarised or parked unit of the project holds, an archive is never replaced, and the record carries id and parent.
gap: The parent is optional: the skeleton sets it to null and no command, validation or gate asks for it, so a record normally names no parent request or workstream.
fix: Require a parent request or workstream id at contract init.

how: The record carries the goal and the scope; a contract needs a non-empty goal, the before-tool guard refuses a placeholder goal, and the scope's shape is validated.
gap: Scope is never asked for: it defaults to empty in and out lists and no gate or guard refuses a unit without it, so the outcome is enforced but the scope is not.
fix: Require a non-empty scope at contract init, refusing it when empty.

how: The contract's requirement list (explicit, implied, contextual, anticipated, experiential, each with a decision) is validated and archived; the gate and the before-tool guard demand it for integration-and-above units and refuse placeholder text.
gap: Required only at integration and above: an isolated or logic unit closes with an empty requirements list and nothing asks.
fix: Require a requirement list for isolated and logic units, not only integration and above.

how: Every contract needs at least one check that can fail (constant-true commands are refused) and the record keeps the checks, the invariants and each one's standing result; invariants are demanded for integration-and-above units.
gap: Invariants are optional below integration: an isolated or logic unit records an empty invariant list and nothing asks whether something important must not get worse.
fix: Require invariants at every profile, not only integration and above.

how: A contract must declare a risk profile (the skeleton pre-fills the measured floor), the gate names a missing one, and the record keeps the floor from the changed paths beside the declared profile, the reason, blast radius, rollback and whether a stronger technique was used.
The record carries the contract's plan and the workers the delegation ledger has for the project inside the unit's window, plus the orchestration telemetry.
gap: The plan is optional (nothing asks for it; the default is an empty list), dependencies have no field at all, and tools or agents used outside a recorded delegation are not listed as assigned.
fix: Add dependencies field and require plan and tools to be recorded.

how: The models used are taken from the host transcript's usage inside the unit's window; budgets are copied from the contract.
gap: Budgets have no mechanism: no skeleton field, no validation, nothing asks, so a record normally has budgets null. Model selection is only what a transcript shows and is empty without one.
fix: Add budgets field to skeleton and validate it is filled.

how: A unit stamps its own start; close stamps the end; build_telemetry derives the times, checks, waits, tokens, delegations and file counts, each classed measured, inferred, estimated or unavailable, never a guessed zero.
Changed artifacts (files and lines since the start commit) are measured with git and kept in the record; the implementation summary is copied from the contract.
gap: The implementation summary has no mechanism: no skeleton field, no validation, nothing asks, so a record normally has summary null.
fix: Add implementation summary field to skeleton and require it at close.

how: Every result of the unit (check, invariant, risk floor, enforced item) with its status, reason, duration and evidence is archived as verification, and each check's standing result is kept, a check with no record shown as not-run.

The record keeps the deferred items (what, why, safe_because, validated), the checks still deferred or needing a human, the mandatory checks that never ran, the limitations and the open risks; such a unit cannot close as plainly delivered.
gap: Known limitations and unresolved risks are kept only when the agent volunteers them: limitations is optional and open_risks is not validated or asked for by anything.
fix: Require limitations and open_risks fields in the contract and validate them.

how: decide_status derives one of five delivery statuses from the unit's results, deviations, gate release or abandonment; close refuses while a check blocks, and the status is stored in the record and the summary line.

build_record stores an eight-dimension scorecard in the archived unit record (every value classed measured/inferred/estimated/unavailable) and the summary line carries it to the user store. The test asserts the key and the eight dimension names on a real close.

The record holds the unit's retro findings in full (retro_findings, from the findings store) and the ids of the learnings the unit created (learning_ids). The test checks one recorded finding reaches the record and that the learning_ids key exists.
gap: The learning records themselves are not in the unit record, only their ids (the records stay in the user store); no test checks that a learning created by the unit's own finding is listed in learning_ids, only that the key is present.
fix: Test that a unit's own finding-created learning id appears in learning_ids.

how: This is the lead-in sentence ('A work unit is complete only when:') for criteria R-10.3-2 to R-10.3-7, which are graded separately; it states no requirement of its own.
gap: None for this line; the completion criteria it introduces are graded as R-10.3-2 to R-10.3-7.

how: A unit cannot close as delivered while a contract check fails, and `sisi unit close --abandon "<reason>"` records an explicit resolution. The outcome itself is stood in for by the contract's checks; the goal, the requirement list and the implementation summary are whatever the agent wrote.
gap: Nothing checks that the stated goal was implemented or explicitly resolved: passing checks are the only proxy, and no check ties the goal or the requirements to what was delivered.
fix: No code can confirm the goal was implemented; ask the agent to state it.

how: close_unit refuses to close a unit as delivered while an acceptance check blocks (test_a_failing_check_refuses_a_close_as_delivered). A waived check closes the unit as `deviation` with the reason recorded and the close message saying the report must say so.
gap: A deviation is recorded by the agent alone: no authorized party's acceptance is required or recorded before the unit is closed, so a unit can be complete with unmet criteria on the agent's own waiver.
fix: Require an owner acknowledgement recorded before a deviation can close the unit.

how: close_unit refuses a close as delivered when a blocking result stands, and mandatory checks that never ran close only as `delivered-with-deferred` (tests test_a_failing_check_refuses_a_close_as_delivered, test_deferred_and_human_checks_close_as_delivered_with_deferred).
gap: The close judges the recorded results, not the tree as it stands: an edit made after the last pass is not detected at close (verified_for_tree exists but is used only by the commit notice in sisi/watch.py).
fix: At close, compare verified tree hash with current tree and refuse if edited.

how: The close tells the agent about a recorded deviation and lists deferred checks, and the record archives limitations, deferred items, never-run mandatory checks, deviations and open risks taken from the contract.
gap: Limitations and open risks are in the record only if the agent wrote them into the contract; nothing decides which failures or limitations are material, requires any to be stated, or checks that the final report discloses them.
fix: Deciding which failures are material is judgement; ask for a disclosure in the report.

how: build_record archives the execution evidence with the unit: every verification result, telemetry (times, tokens, delegations, orchestration), changed artifacts from git, start and closing commits and guard refusals, with missing data marked unavailable. The tests assert these keys on a real close and check the changed artifacts' content.
