At the end of a turn, with everything green, the gate closes the unit only when a finding is recorded and otherwise sends the agent back once per state of the tree with the retro (sisi/gate.py:399-413). A trivial unit is asked nothing unless it shows an anomaly.
gap: The analysis is asked for, not made a condition of closing: `sisi unit close` archives a unit with no finding at all (many tests close units this way), and after the single offer the gate lets the turn end with the unit still open.
fix: Refuse unit close when no retro finding is recorded, as the gate already does.

how: `sisi unit close --abandon "<reason>"` stops a unit: it requires a reason, and the record carries delivery status `abandoned` with the reason. The test checks that no reason is refused and that the reason is recorded.
The end-of-turn gate asks for a retro (one send-back per state of the tree) and closes the unit once a finding is recorded for it; a recorded finding is the only thing it checks for.
gap: Not every unit gets a review: `sisi unit close` archives a unit with no finding at all (sisi/unit.py:648), a second stop with no new edit passes silently after the one offer (sisi/gate.py:409), and config `retro.required` switches the ask off (sisi/gate.py:407).
fix: Retro is skippable via retro.required config and unit close; forbid the switch-off.

how: Every closed unit gets an eight-dimension scorecard built by `scorecard.build_scorecard` from the record (checks, transcript, ledger, git), each value classed measured/inferred/estimated/unavailable; `sisi retro` prints it for the open unit.

`unit.summary_for_retro` prints what stands out in the record: checks that failed then passed, still failing, never ran, a deviation, human corrections, gate send-backs, unavailable measures; the scorecard counts requirements added after the first verification.
gap: Only what the record already holds is surfaced; wasted effort and missed opportunities are not detected anywhere, and a clean unit prints 'nothing in the record stands out'. The finding itself is whatever the agent types.
fix: Spotting waste and surprises needs judgement; ask the retro to address each category explicitly.

how: `sisi retro --disposition promote` is refused without `--change`, and a change made only of filler words is refused as generic.
gap: Only a `promote` finding needs a recommendation. A unit closes on one `record` or `drop` finding that proposes no way the outcome or process could have been better.
fix: Require a concrete recommendation field on record and drop findings too.

how: A finding is refused unless `--cause` is given (at least 8 characters, not filler-only).
gap: Nothing checks that the cause is a cause: a cause that restates the symptom, or 20 arbitrary letters, is accepted. `sisi rule 8` itself lists 'names a root cause' as left to the agent.
fix: Whether a cause is a true root cause cannot be checked by code; ask for it.

how: `learning.earned_scope` decides from provenance whether a learning reaches beyond its own task: only after it is seen in two units in two projects, or as an owner statement; a cycle that asks for more waits for the owner (sisi/cycle.py:517).

`cycle._apply_mechanism` installs a proposed learning as a persistent mechanism in the user store (enforced check, contract requirement, rule sentence, library entry, risk or routing adjustment, benchmark), stamped with the learning id, its earned scope and origin project, and read back filtered by project.

A promoted command check is replayed between the unit's start and closing commits and must fail before and pass after; what cannot be shown waits for the owner and is never called validated. Approved changes are applied by `sisi approve` and enforced in later sessions.
gap: Only command checks are validated. Risk, routing, contract-requirement, benchmark and rule changes take effect at once with result `unvalidated` (sisi/cycle.py:577, sisi/cycle.py:782), so an accepted improvement is not necessarily a validated one.
fix: Validate all mechanism kinds by replay or evaluation before they take effect.

how: `learning.is_generic` refuses text made only of filler words; `sisi retro` applies it to the finding, the cause and the change, and the cycle to a rule sentence and a reject reason.
For a non-trivial unit the gate withholds the end of the turn until at least one finding is recorded for it.
gap: One finding of any kind counts: a `drop` with no improvement, or a recurrence of an old learning. `sisi unit close` archives with none, trivial units are asked nothing, and a fully green unit is not asked for a way it could have scored better.
fix: Require a finding that names an improvement even when the unit succeeded.

how: A `promote` finding is refused unless it names the change, the mechanism, the expected effect and how it will be tested.
gap: `record` and `drop` findings need none of the three, yet they are what lets a unit close, so an opportunity can be written with no action, effect or validation.
fix: Apply the action, effect and validation requirement to record and drop findings.

how: The cycle brief orders the learnings it shows: flagged first, then the most recurrent, then the oldest.
gap: Priority rests on recurrence and age only. Expected value, implementation cost and risk are never estimated, and confidence is a fixed label ('low', 'high' for owner statements: sisi/learning.py:501).
fix: Add expected value, cost and risk fields and order learnings by them.

how: A `drop` is refused without `--why-not`, and a cycle `reject` without a specific reason; a short specific finding is accepted where an invented generic one is refused.
gap: The drop reason is demanded but not recorded: the row written to findings.jsonl carries no reason field (sisi/retro.py:177; confirmed by running it), the reason is not checked for genericness, and nothing stops a low-value change being written as a `promote`.
fix: Store the drop reason in findings.jsonl and check it is not generic.

how: A recorded finding is appended to findings.jsonl and committed in the user store, and the archived unit record lists the unit's findings and the learnings they made.
gap: It exists only when a finding is recorded. `sisi unit close` archives a unit with no finding (tests/test_unit.py::test_close_archives_all_fourteen_items closes one that way) and trivial units are never asked.
fix: Refuse unit close without a recorded finding so every unit writes a review artifact.

how: `learning.delivery_text` adds learnings in scope to later prompts and `cycle.enforced_results` runs enforced mechanisms, both filtered by the scope the learning earned (its project until seen in two projects; owner statements at user scope).
gap: Only project, user and organization scope have an effect: `task-class` is stored as a label and never acts and there is no workstream scope (sisi/learning.py:22, sisi/cycle.py:519). A unit closed on a single `drop` finding makes no learning available at all.
fix: Implement workstream and task-class scopes so they change what is delivered.

how: A `record` finding is refused without `--limits`, and the finding, cause and limits are stored as a learning record with status `observed`.
gap: No test records a finding without `--limits`, so removing the refusal would fail nothing, and the limits text is not checked for substance (`--limits x` is accepted; confirmed by running it).
fix: Add a test that a record finding without --limits is refused.

how: `sisi retro` prints the unit's scorecard and what stands out, which covers results, late requirements, corrections, send-backs, time in checks and waits, tokens, delegations and overlap.
gap: Nothing checks that the questions are considered: assumptions, context loading, model choice, what could have been automated and future change cost are not surfaced, and a finding is accepted without addressing any question.
fix: Whether each retro question was considered is judgement; ask the retro to answer each.

how: The scorecard's intent dimension counts requirements with a passing check, requirements added late and human corrections inferred from the transcript, and `sisi retro` prints it beside the unit's goal.
gap: The question is never asked or answered on record: a unit whose requirements have no check shows unavailable and still closes as delivered, and no test asserts this dimension in the retro output.
fix: Whether the result solved the user's problem needs the owner's judgement; ask for a recorded answer.

how: `sisi retro` prints the scorecard's intent fulfilment line (requirements added after the first verification, requirements with a passing check, human corrections), which is the data for this question.
gap: Nothing asks or checks that this question was considered: the retro can be one finding about anything, the gate offers the retro once per tree state and then lets the turn end, and no test covers the late-requirements count.
fix: Missed requirements are a judgement; require an explicit answer field in the retro.

how: The contract stores an `assumptions` list (sisi/contract.py:79), but `sisi retro` never prints it, the scorecard has no value for it and nothing compares the assumptions with what happened.
gap: No mechanism, measure or check for wrong or useful assumptions; rule 8 does not mention them either.
fix: Print contract assumptions in the retro and require a useful or wrong verdict for each.

how: The retro prints unit-level time and cost totals only; nothing attributes cost or delay to a decision, and the contract's `approach` (chosen, why, alternatives) is never looked at again.
gap: No mechanism, measure or check for decisions that were unnecessarily expensive or slow.
fix: Attribute cost and delay to recorded decisions; nothing currently links them.

how: `unit.build_telemetry` measures time in checks, in waits (pauses), in delegations, time to first useful result and to completion, and the number of send-backs; `sisi retro` prints them as the delivery velocity line.
gap: No separate figures for execution, integration or queueing, and nothing checks that the retro considered where time went; the gate offers the retro once and then lets the turn end.
fix: Print execution, integration and queueing figures alongside the existing time totals.

how: The retro's parallelism and resource lines show delegations started, judged and unjudged, the delegated share of tool calls and tokens by model; the judged record of workers is kept by `sisi delegate judge`.
gap: Counts and model names only: nothing says whether a choice was right, the judgement is left to the agent, and nothing checks that the question was considered.
fix: Right model choice is a judgement; ask the retro to answer it per delegation.

how: The scorecard's parallelism dimension records delegations, overlapping delegations, worker minutes and wall time, and `sisi retro` prints it.
gap: Nothing measures coordination cost against the benefit (no critical path before and after), and nothing checks that the retro considered it.
fix: Compute critical path before and after delegation to show whether parallelism helped.

how: The retro prints tokens by category and by model from the host transcript, and the characters read by the main thread's own tool calls (orchestration telemetry).
gap: Totals per unit only: nothing separates context loaded once from context re-sent, nothing flags inefficient delegation, and nothing checks that the question was considered.
fix: Detect context re-sent across turns and flag inefficient delegation patterns.

how: The retro's correctness line prints the techniques used, whether any check is stronger than examples, the checks seen failing and independent evidence; the gate notes once when no check is stronger than examples.
gap: Too broad or redundant verification is not in the retro (time saved by selection and reuse is printed by `sisi verify` only), and nothing checks that the question was considered.
fix: Too-weak or too-broad verification is judgement; ask the retro to answer it.

how: `sisi retro` lists human corrections and mandatory checks that never ran; `sisi escapes` lists candidate cases where verified work was later corrected; the unit record keeps open risks, limitations and deferred checks.
gap: `sisi escapes` is a separate command over the transcript database that the agent must remember to run and that no test covers; the retro itself raises no escaped defect.
fix: Run sisi escapes automatically in the retro and add a test covering it.

how: The scorecard's lifecycle quality line, printed by `sisi retro`, records files and lines changed, whether tests changed with code and whether public surface was touched.
gap: No test asserts those four values, nothing measures change cost beyond size, and nothing checks that the question was considered.
fix: Add a test asserting the four lifecycle quality values appear in the retro.

how: I looked in the retro, the scorecard and the gate for anything about what could have been anticipated or automated and found none; rule 8 does not mention it.
gap: No mechanism, measure or check.
fix: What could have been anticipated or automated is judgement; ask for it in the retro.

how: `sisi retro --disposition promote` refuses a finding without a root cause, the exact change, a mechanism type, an expected effect and a validation method.
gap: A retro may consist of a single `record` or `drop` finding that names no mechanism, and nothing checks that this question was answered.
fix: Require a mechanism field on every finding, including record and drop.

how: A promoted finding must name a root cause, a mechanism of one of eight kinds and the exact change, and a generic cause or change is refused.
gap: Nothing can check that the mechanism addresses the cause rather than the symptom: that choice is the agent's (then the cycle worker's).
fix: Whether a mechanism addresses the cause rather than the symptom needs judgement.

how: `sisi cycle apply` writes a promoted mechanism into the user store where code reads it without the agent: enforced checks are run by `sisi verify` (cycle.enforced_results), rule additions join the generated rulebook every session loads, risk and routing adjustments are read by `sisi risk` and `sisi route`; each is filtered to the scope the learning earned.

`learning.new_record` writes one JSON record per learning with id, title, source unit, observation (evidence, impact), root cause, proposed change (description, mechanism, scope), expected effect, validation (method, benchmark, result), status, version, provenance and confidence; the version is bumped on promotion and the user store is a git repository.
gap: No test asserts the field set: only status, validation result, provenance and terms are checked, so removing root cause, expected effect or method would pass; the validation benchmark is never filled in.
fix: Add a test asserting root cause, expected effect and validation fields are present.

how: A MAY that leaves the storage choice open and asks nothing of the product; sisi uses files (learnings.jsonl in the user store's git repository).
gap: None: the text only permits a storage choice.

how: Every learning has a status from a fixed list (`STATUSES`) and sisi's commands move it: observed, proposed or backlog at creation, pending-approval or promoted by the cycle, monitored once a unit in scope closes, and revised, reverted, rejected or merged.
gap: `analyzed`, `implemented` and `validated` are in the list but no live command sets them: a promote finding is created directly as `proposed` and becomes `promoted` in one cycle step (validation is a result field, not a state).
fix: Set analyzed, implemented and validated in the live flow, or drop them from the list.

how: A finding recorded with `--disposition record` creates a learning whose status is `observed`, and every finding is appended to findings.jsonl with its unit and project.

`sisi retro` refuses a finding without a non-generic --cause and a promote without --expect, and the scope in force is computed by learning.earned_scope from provenance. But no learning ever holds the state `analyzed`: the retro writes `observed` or `proposed` directly.
gap: The explicit `analyzed` state is never assigned in the live flow (it is only a name in the status list), so nothing records or checks that analysis finished as its own step; --scope is optional and defaults to project.
fix: Set the analyzed state in the live flow and require --scope rather than default it.

how: `sisi retro --disposition promote` refuses a finding without --change, a --mechanism from the fixed list, --expect and --validate, and learning.new_record stores it with status `proposed` and the defined change (description, mechanism, scope, target); the cycle brief lists only `proposed` learnings.

The cycle writes each mechanism as data the code evaluates (a command with an expected exit, a contract requirement with a risk profile or path glob) in _apply_mechanism, but the live flow never assigns the state `implemented`: a `proposed` learning becomes `promoted` in the step that writes the mechanism.
gap: No `implemented` state in the live cycle (only the migration sets it, sisi/lifecycle.py:421), and a rule sentence, library entry, routing or benchmark change is promoted without ever existing in a testable form.
fix: Assign the implemented state when a mechanism is written to its testable form.

how: cycle.replay_validate calls evaluate.validate_command, which replays a command check between the learning's own unit commits and reports `validated` only when it ran and failed before the fix and passed after. Nothing else is evaluated.
gap: Only the original scenario, only for command checks: no regression cases are run, the other mechanism kinds are promoted with result `unvalidated`, and the status `validated` itself is never assigned (the record goes to `promoted` or `pending-approval`).
fix: Evaluate every mechanism kind against original scenario and regression cases before promotion.

how: _apply_mechanism writes each mechanism with the learning id, its granted scope and origin project; entry_applies and load_enforced(project) let it reach only its project unless the learning earned more or the owner approved, and verify, risk and routing read them per project.

learning.monitor moves a promoted learning to `monitored` once a unit in its scope has closed or it recurred; add_recurrence counts recurrences after promotion and learning_report prints, per learning, the units since, the recurrences and a verdict.
gap: What is observed is only whether the same finding recurred and how many units closed. The learning's expected effect is free text that nothing measures, so a positive effect is never observed, only the absence of recurrence.
fix: Measure the expected effect of a promoted learning, not only absence of recurrence.

how: Two recurrences flag a learning and validate_doc refuses a cycle file that leaves a flagged learning without a revise or revert action; _apply_status sets `revised` or `reverted` and _remove_mechanisms deletes its enforced, risk and routing entries.
gap: _remove_mechanisms (sisi/cycle.py:701) does not remove a sentence the learning added to a rule, a library entry or a benchmark case, so those stay in force after a per-learning revert; only a whole-cycle revert reaches them. A flagged learning is acted on only if an agent runs a cycle, which session start merely announces.
fix: Remove sentences a learning added to rules, library and benchmarks on per-learning revert.

how: _plan_promote collects the reasons a change is consequential; when there are none, apply_file writes the mechanism at once with no owner decision (a risk pattern that does not lower, routing, benchmark, a contract requirement, a replayed command check, and rule-add or library once scope is earned).

A cycle cannot touch the rules in canon/protected.json at all, even after approval. A whole-rule replacement, disabling a rule, more scope than earned, an unreplayed command and a risk pattern that lowers a profile are parked and take effect only through `sisi approve`, which needs a word typed at the controlling terminal and is refused when an agent's shell invokes it.
gap: Stronger validation exists only for command checks (the replay). A rule change that waits for the owner is checked for format, sentence count and rulebook size only: no evaluation against cases is run or required before approval, and nothing maps a change to a security boundary or to destructive behaviour onto a check beyond these kinds.
fix: Require evaluation against cases before approving security or destructive policy changes.

how: learning.earned_scope keeps a learning at project scope unless its provenance holds at least two units in at least two projects (or it is an owner statement); a unit is counted once per learning, entry_applies lets a mechanism reach only where that scope reaches, and a rule sentence from a one-project learning waits for the owner.

new_record stores a scope from a fixed list (organization, user, project, task-class) and earned_scope decides what is in force: organization only from two units in two projects, user for an owner statement made at that scope, else the origin project.
gap: Task-specific is not determined. `task-class` is accepted by `sisi retro --scope` but earned_scope never returns it, the cycle refuses that value (sisi/cycle.py:519), and such a learning is delivered like any project-wide one.
fix: Make earned_scope return task-class and let the cycle accept it.

how: A command check is replayed against the originating task (the two commits of its unit). The evaluation harness separately holds cases from closed units with dev, holdout and counterexample splits and can replay a stored check at its two commits.
gap: Promotion (cycle._plan_promote) runs only the one-command replay of the original scenario. Nothing runs a new mechanism against similar historical cases, held-out cases or counterexamples: evaluate.validate_check and select_cases have no caller in the cycle.
fix: Run each new mechanism against similar historical, held-out and counterexample cases.

how: evaluate.compare_for_candidate (`sisi eval shadow DIR`) runs the same dev and counterexample cases under the current and the candidate policy and compares them by policy version, never running holdout cases.
gap: It is not used for consequential changes. cycle.apply_pending and cmd_approve never call it: the module docstring says the approval path calls it, but its only caller is the `sisi eval shadow` command, so a comparison happens only if someone chooses to run it. There is no canary rollout.
fix: Call compare_for_candidate from cycle approval for consequential changes.

how: unit.policy_version hashes the rulebook, both risk tables, the enforced checks and the gate/verify config into each unit record's policy_version, and each learning and mechanism entry carries its provenance (units, projects, learning id, scope).
gap: The version is a hash with no way back: nothing records or resolves which rulebook text and which mechanisms a version stands for. Routing adjustments, library entries and benchmark cases are outside the hash, so two units with different routing mechanisms share a version.
fix: Store and resolve the rulebook and mechanisms behind each policy version hash.

how: cycle.revert_cycle puts back every file one cycle changed and the learning fields it changed, drops the decisions it parked, and refuses when a later change touched the same file; a learning's own revert or revise removes its enforced, risk and routing entries, and _transact restores the store if an apply fails part-way.

Some pieces exist as mechanisms: a generic finding or cause is refused (learning.is_generic), a finding that resembles a learning is attached as a recurrence and a merge folds duplicates, and a command check is replayed in an exported copy under a time limit instead of in the working tree.
gap: Nothing learns to score more reliably or to find stronger root causes: the scorecard, the risk table and the retro's cause check are fixed code with no feedback from later units, and no measure of scoring reliability or root-cause quality exists. Self-evaluation bias is not measured either. The improvement system changes only through tool learnings a person later applies.
fix: Feed later unit outcomes back into scoring and root-cause checks, measuring their reliability.

how: overlay.protected_rules reads canon/protected.json and fails closed; a cycle, `sisi overlay` and even an approval cannot replace or disable those rules, and the product layer is never written at run time.
gap: The rule that states the objective (`own-the-outcome`) is not in canon/protected.json. Once a learning has earned scope, a cycle adds one or two sentences to it with no owner decision, and only their form is checked, not whether they change the objective's order or limits.
fix: Add the objective statement in core.md to canon/protected.json so cycles cannot change it.

how: A change to sisi itself is a `tool` learning held on the backlog, never applied by a cycle, and `sisi promote --export` writes it as a scrubbed contribution file that is sent nowhere; `sisi promote L-NNNN --apply` writes the text into the product folder as an uncommitted edit.
gap: Owner review is not enforced for `sisi promote --apply`: any session in the clone can run it (it only needs the source folder; there is no terminal word and no hook refusal, unlike `sisi approve`). There is no separate version of the objective or of the evaluation model, only the learning's version counter and git.
fix: Require the owner's typed word for sisi promote --apply, as sisi approve does.

how: Learnings and owner statements are written to the user store by `sisi retro --finding` and `sisi learn` (learning.new_record) and handed to later sessions on each request by learning.delivery_text through prompt.build_context. The tests check that a recorded learning is delivered to a matching later request and that `sisi learn` stores what `sisi oracle` prints.

Scope is earned, not claimed (earned_scope, in_scope): a learning is delivered only in the project it came from unless it was seen in two units in two projects or is an owner statement at user scope, secrets are scrubbed before storage, and handover items are shown only in their project. The tests check that a one-unit learning and a project-scoped statement are not delivered in another project.
This is the lead-in line ('Recommended logical layers are:') for the six layers graded as R-12-4 to R-12-9; it states no requirement of its own.
gap: None for this line; the layers it introduces are graded as R-12-4 to R-12-9.

how: The product folder is this layer: canon/ holds the rulebook, the routing and risk tables and the skills, read at run time (policy_version hashes the rulebook and risk tables), and `sisi promote` / `--export` is the only way a user's learning reaches it, scrubbed. The tests scan the product for owner-specific material (test_no_owner_specific_or_perishable_material) and check the promote and export paths (which I did not open).
gap: No shared benchmarks live in this layer (evaluation cases are captured into the user store), and no test checks that the layer holds the items the text lists.
fix: Add a test that the organization-wide layer holds each item the text lists.

how: `sisi learn [--scope user|project|organization]` stores an owner's preference as a statement in the user store, `sisi oracle` prints it, and it is delivered to later sessions at its scope. The test checks that a statement is stored once and printed back; a second test checks scope separation.

The project keeps its open contract, its closed unit records and its risk overrides under .sisi/, and project-scoped learnings are listed by `sisi handover` for filing into the project's own documents. The tests check that the handover lists only this project's items and is shown once per session.
gap: Architecture, conventions, decisions and the like are not stored by the product: they reach the project's documents only when an agent acts on the handover notice, so the layer rests on the agent following advice.
fix: Project architecture and conventions are the agent's to record; the product cannot check content.

how: I looked for any structure that holds a workstream's initiative, plans, interfaces, unresolved decisions or dependencies across units and found none: the word workstream appears in no module, and a unit only carries a free-text `parent` id.
gap: There is no workstream layer: nothing stores or retrieves a workstream's plan, interfaces, open decisions or dependencies between units; only the unit's parent id links it to a request.
fix: Add a workstream record holding plan, interfaces, open decisions and dependencies across units.

how: The open contract (.sisi/contract.json) is the unit's working state: goal, requirements, assumptions, questions, deferred items, plan and pauses; it can be parked and resumed, and the whole contract is archived with the unit. Contract validation and the pause test cover parts of it.
gap: Discoveries and intermediate outputs have no place of their own, the fields are filled only by what the agent writes, and no test checks that the archived unit keeps its assumptions or plan.
fix: Test that the archived unit keeps its assumptions and plan.

how: A cycle turns a learning into something the product executes: risk patterns risk.py reads, routing adjustments `sisi route` reads, and enforced contract requirements and command checks that verify runs (cycle.py routing_adjustments, risk_patterns, load_enforced, enforced_results). The test shows a promoted learning changing `sisi route` in its own project only.

learning.new_record gives every learning provenance (unit, project, time), a created time, a version, a scope, a confidence label and a limits field; the version is raised when a cycle revises it. The tests check the stored text, scope and withdraw path of an owner statement.
gap: There is no supersession information (nothing says which item a learning replaces or what replaced it), validity conditions are filled only when a retro uses the `record` disposition, and confidence is a fixed label (high for an owner statement, low otherwise) rather than an assessed value.
fix: Add a supersedes field to learning records and show it in the learning report.

how: A finding that resembles an existing learning is attached to it as a recurrence instead of being added as a duplicate, and two recurrences after promotion flag it not working so the next cycle must revise or revert it; an owner statement can be withdrawn. Tests cover the resemblance and the flagging.
gap: Nothing detects contradictory learnings or statements, and staleness is detected only for worker facts and for a promoted learning that recurs twice; an old learning that is merely out of date is combined with the rest.
fix: Detect contradictory learnings and stale items rather than combining them silently.

how: learning.delivery_text returns only learnings in scope whose terms match the request (at most a few), and prompt.build_context injects nothing for a trivial request and caps the text. The tests check that relevance is scored against the learning's own terms on a long prompt and that a typo-fix request gets no injection.

`sisi unit close` builds and stores an eight-dimension scorecard per unit (scorecard.build_scorecard) and `sisi status` prints per-segment median/p95 trends by project, risk profile, model and policy version (scorecard.trends). There is no segment by agent, risk profile stands in for task class, and each figure is a median over all units of a segment with no time dimension.
gap: No trend by agent; task class is approximated by risk profile; nothing shows a segment improving or deteriorating over time.
fix: Add trends by agent and over time, with task class separate from risk profile.

how: The unit scorecard records pieces of eight derived measures, but only recurrence counts and a realization proxy are computed; rework rate, cost per accepted change, verification efficiency, delegation benefit and first-pass acceptance are never derived.
gap: Five of the eight listed measures are not derived at all (see R-13.2-3 to R-13.2-6, R-13.2-9).
fix: Derive rework rate, cost per accepted change, verification efficiency, delegation benefit and first-pass acceptance.

how: The scorecard counts requirements whose `added` stamp is later than the first recorded result (requirements_added_after_first_verification). sisi never writes that stamp (it is only validated in contract.py), no rate or impact is derived, and no test exercises the value.
gap: Depends on the agent hand-writing `added`; it is a raw count with no rate, no impact and no test.
fix: Derive a surprise rate from the added stamp and a test covering the value.

how: I looked for anything that computes the share of work repeated or corrected: send-backs and inferred human corrections are stored as separate telemetry values, but no rework rate is derived or reported anywhere.
gap: No rework rate is computed from the recorded corrections, send-backs or retries.
fix: Derive rework rate from send-backs and inferred corrections over total units.

how: An estimated cost per unit is derived from measured tokens and recorded price facts (unit._estimated_cost), and each unit has a delivery status; nothing counts accepted changes or divides cost by them.
gap: No numerator/denominator: cost per accepted change is never computed or reported.
fix: Divide unit cost by accepted-change count and report the cost per accepted change.

how: scorecard.check_stats reports per check its runs, failures and total seconds (`sisi checks`), and each result stores its duration; no measure relates defects found to elapsed time or cost.
gap: Inputs are tabulated, but no verification efficiency (risk reduction or defects found per time or cost) is derived.
fix: Relate defects found to elapsed time and cost to derive verification efficiency.

how: The ledger yields worker minutes against wall time and the number of overlapping delegation pairs (workers.delegations_for_project), stored in the scorecard's parallelism dimension. Nothing compares wall time with expected serial execution or offsets it by coordination and integration effort.
gap: No critical-path reduction or coordination/integration offset is computed; only overlap counts and minutes.
fix: Compare wall time with expected serial time, offset by coordination and integration effort.

how: learning.learning_report prints the share of promoted learnings with no recurrence over at least five units in scope, or 'too few'. That is an absence-of-recurrence proxy: the learning's expected effect is never checked, and only the 'too few' branch is tested.
gap: Realization is inferred from no recurrence, not from the expected effect; the numeric rate line has no test.
fix: Add a test for the numeric realization rate line.

how: learning.add_recurrence counts a recurrence once per unit against a promoted learning and flags it after two; the learning report shows units since promotion against recurrences, and the unit scorecard carries a `recurrences` count. The per-unit scorecard value has no test and no rate is aggregated.
gap: Counts per learning and per unit are kept, but no recurrence rate is derived, and the scorecard's `recurrences` value is untested.
fix: Aggregate recurrences over promoted learnings into a rate and test it.

how: Per-unit inferred human corrections, question dialogs and delivery status are recorded in the scorecard, and `sisi escapes` lists units that passed verification and were then corrected (scorecard.escape_candidates). Nothing derives the proportion of units accepted without material correction or avoidable rework, and the escape candidates have no test.
gap: No first-pass acceptance proportion is computed or reported.
fix: Compute the share of units accepted without correction and test it.

how: Trends are segmented by project, risk profile, model and policy version (scorecard.trends); only the delegation ledger's judged record is broken down by task type and difficulty. The derived metrics are not segmented by task category and complexity.
gap: No segmentation of the metrics by task category or complexity.
fix: Break derived metrics down by task category and complexity alongside existing trends.

how: Each segment is reported on its own line with median and p95, segments under five units say 'too few', and no cross-segment score is computed or printed. The segments are not task categories, and a per-segment median over all units has no time axis, so one category improving while another deteriorates still cannot be seen.
gap: No per-category or per-time view: a split inside a segment (one task class up, another down) is still concealed.
fix: Add per-category and over-time views so a split inside a segment is visible.

how: scorecard.build_scorecard combines transcript and hook telemetry, git changes, verification results, an independent-evidence flag and inferred human corrections. Two of the four sources are thin: independent evidence is a self-declared flag and outcome evidence stops at corrections.
gap: Independent evaluation and outcome evidence are only partly combined (see R-13.3-4 and R-13.3-5).
fix: Combine independent evaluation and outcome evidence into the scoring.

how: unit.build_telemetry and the orchestration meter record start/end times, tokens by category and model, the models used, estimated cost, send-backs, check durations, delegation counts and every tool call with its tool name; build_scorecard folds them into the unit record.
gap: Overturned by the audit: The unit record keeps only counts (direct_calls, delegations), not each tool call with its name or the commands run (the shell note says command text is not kept), and the named test covers only tokens by category/model and cost, so the full list of telemetry items is neither recorded nor tested.

how: The scorecard takes artifact evidence from git (files and lines changed, tests changed with code, public surface) and from recorded test results by status; build outputs, static analysis and proofs appear only as whatever a check's result row holds, and benchmark cases are captured at close but not scored. No deployment records are scored.
gap: Only diff size and test results reach the scorecard; build outputs, analysis, proofs, benchmarks and deployment records do not.
fix: Score build outputs, analysis, proofs, benchmarks and deployment records as artifact evidence.

how: For data, critical and release units the gate demands independent evidence and assure.independent_evidence refuses evidence by the author (self-reference or the session's own model); the scorecard's own independent_evidence value, however, counts any check flagged `independent` that passed, without that test.
gap: The scorecard (the scoring) accepts the author's own `independent` flag; no test covers that value; lower profiles need no independent evaluation at all.
fix: Apply the author test to the scorecard's independent_evidence value and cover it by a test.

how: The scorecard records inferred human corrections and question dialogs from the transcript, plus delivery status and deviation/unverified flags. Nothing records user acceptance, incidents, subsequent changes or production behaviour.
gap: Outcome evidence is limited to transcript corrections; no acceptance, incident, later-change or production outcome is captured or scored.
fix: Capture user acceptance, incidents and later changes as outcome evidence in the record.

how: Objective values come from executed checks, the transcript and hooks rather than from the agent's say-so, and the gate sends back a data/critical/release unit whose only evidence is the author's own (assure.independent_evidence, unitguard.is_self_reference). But a check the agent ran itself counts if `by` names anything that is not the author, the scorecard counts the bare `independent` flag, and below `data` the agent is the only source.
gap: Independence of a flagged check rests on the agent's own `by` text; the scorecard's independent_evidence value applies no author test; isolated, logic and integration units need no second source.
fix: Below data profile the agent is the only source by design; a profile change, not code.

how: scorecard.val and build_scorecard give every per-unit scorecard value one of measured, inferred, estimated or unavailable, and unit.build_telemetry classes each telemetry value the same way; sisi status prints the class beside each value. The trend tables in sisi status (scorecard.trends) print medians and p95 with no class at all.
gap: Trend medians and p95 in sisi status carry no confidence class and pool measured with inferred values, so not every score shown indicates its class.
fix: Print the confidence class beside each trend median and p95 in sisi status.

how: Missing telemetry is built as {value None, class unavailable}: with no transcript or no usage numbers, tokens, cost and human counts are never zero (unit.build_telemetry), scorecard.trends drops unavailable values instead of counting them, and evaluation never treats an unavailable cost as zero or cheap. Percentiles are only printed from five or more units.

Missing data is named rather than hidden: unavailable classes and a 'not measurable here' line in the retro summary, a one-line warning at session start when the hooks are not wired (pointing to sisi doctor), and a doctor report of what each tool's hooks can measure. Nothing adds instrumentation in response to a score that cannot be evaluated; that is left to the agent.
gap: No mechanism improves observability when missing data prevents evaluation; sisi only reports the missing data and broken wiring.
fix: Adding instrumentation for unscoreable work is the agent's judgement; sisi can only report it.

how: No aggregate index is computed or printed: sisi status prints each unit's eight dimensions with their class and delivery status, then trends per segment. The retro, the point where improvement decisions are made, prints the whole scorecard plus what stands out (still failing, checks that never ran, deviations, send-backs, human corrections, what is unavailable), so a decision sees scorecard, gate outcomes, confidence and counter-metrics together.
gap: Overturned by the audit: The mechanism is only the absence of an index plus a retro printout; nothing makes a decision inspect scorecard, gate outcomes, confidence and counter-metrics (the cycle brief does not show them), and the named test only asserts that no overall score appears in status, not that the retro prints the full scorecard.

how: The end-of-turn gate sends the agent back to run the checks and record the retro itself instead of stopping, and one kind of unnecessary question to the human (right after a worker outage) is refused once. Doing investigation, planning and implementation without asking is asked for in rule 1 text only.
gap: Nothing checks or makes the agent investigate, plan or implement on its own; that part rests on the rulebook prose.
fix: Acting independently within permission is judgement; no code can check initiative.

how: Approval boundaries that sisi itself owns are enforced: a pending change is decided only with a word typed at a controlling terminal, and the before-tool hook refuses an agent's shell command that invokes sisi approve. No mechanism recognizes a consequential external action (push, publish, deploy, payment) or stops an agent from taking it on the strength of a build request; rule 9 lists asking first as judgement left to the agent.
gap: Nothing in the code prevents inferring authorization for consequential external actions from a request to build; only sisi's own approval points are protected.
fix: Detect push, publish, deploy and payment actions and require explicit authorization for each.

how: sisi pauses for the owner only for its own consequential changes: replacing or disabling a rule waits for sisi approve, a learned driver that switches off approvals and an allowance probe using a secret wait for the owner, and a contract's commands never run from an untrusted root. No hook or gate pauses a destructive, irreversible, externally visible, financially consequential or privacy-sensitive action by the agent.
gap: The listed action classes (destructive, irreversible, externally visible, financial, security- and privacy-sensitive) are not detected or paused anywhere in the code; only sisi's own policy, driver and probe approvals are.
fix: Detect destructive, irreversible, external, financial and privacy actions and pause for the owner.

how: The question gate sends back a reply that ends by asking the human a question in prose, making the question go through the dialog, and the contract has fields for assumptions and questions. Nothing detects that an ambiguity materially affects the result or risk, and nothing requires a clarification in that case; rule 1 text asks for it.
gap: Recognizing material ambiguity and seeking clarification is not checked by any mechanism; only the channel a question uses is enforced.
fix: Recognising material ambiguity is judgement; the product can only route the question.

how: The non-negotiable constraints are listed in canon/protected.json and overlay.protected_rules fails closed: a cycle, the overlay command and even an owner approval cannot replace or disable them, under new or retired ids. The rulebook, risk tables, enforced checks and gate config are hashed into a policy version stored on every closed unit.

A cycle may propose changes, but replacing or disabling a rule and other consequential changes are parked as pending-approval and take effect only after cycle.cmd_approve, which needs the word it prints typed at a controlling terminal; a process with no terminal is refused and the attempt recorded. The rules that define success and permitted action stay protected even from approval.

cycle._plan_promote works out, per action, the reasons that make it consequential (disabling or replacing a rule, a scope wider than earned, an unvalidated command, a command that would run in every project) and those wait for the owner; every applied change is committed to the user store so revert is exact. Reversibility is not classified: no impact or reversibility label is computed or stored on a change.
gap: Changes are sorted only into consequential or not; there is no classification by reversibility and no stored impact or reversibility class.
fix: Store an impact and reversibility label on each policy change.

how: A failing check does not let the turn end: the gate sends the agent back with the failing check's own output (the failing test and its assertion, not only the tail), the failure and its evidence stay in the record, and after three send-backs the unit is released and recorded as unverified instead of read as done.
This is the lead-in sentence of a list; its only content is the five items graded separately as R-15-3 to R-15-7.
gap: Lead-in fragment with no requirement of its own; see R-15-3 to R-15-7.

how: A unit with no activity for unit.stale_hours (12) is treated as stale and the guard asks for sisi unit continue before more edits; the direct-work budget refuses a main thread that does too much itself until it delegates or records a specific reason. Neither measures progress against an expected interval, and neither makes the agent reassess the approach.
gap: There is no progress-over-time detection: staleness means 12 hours of no activity and the only response is a request to re-bind the unit, not a reassessment or reassignment.
fix: Detect progress over an expected interval and require a reassessment or reassignment.

how: The before-tool hook counts failing shell commands (whitespace-normalised) with no file changed in between; the fourth identical attempt is refused with a message saying it will produce no new information and to diagnose or change the approach. sisi route --retry-of likewise moves retries to a worker with strictly better evidence after two rejections.

workers.classify_failure tells a limit, login, not-installed or connection outage from work that failed on its merits: an outage marks the worker down until its reset time, supersedes the pending run and hands the agent the next worker, while a result that failed on its merits marks nothing down. A passed check is not re-run on identical inputs.

Transparency is kept when a check is waived: the waiver never turns anything green, the unit reads deviation everywhere and the scorecard carries a deviation flag. Nothing isolates an unstable check (no rerun, quarantine or flaky flag), and a failing check can simply be deleted from the contract, after which it no longer speaks for the unit.
gap: No isolation of flaky verification and no record or refusal when a meaningful check is removed from the contract.
fix: Rerun, quarantine or flag unstable checks, and refuse removing a meaningful check silently.

how: The brief template requires a Context and sources of truth part (reported by sisi delegate check as advice), each judgement records the strongest check applied, and sisi delegate amend marks a result that later proved wrong. Nothing detects that two workers' outputs conflict, and nothing resolves a conflict by a source-of-truth hierarchy or an independent check.
gap: Conflicting agent outputs are neither detected nor resolved by a mechanism; the sources-of-truth part of a brief is written advice and independent verification is optional in a contract.
fix: Detect conflicting worker outputs and require an independent check before resolving them.

how: sisi recognises the signals of a scope or specification error and makes them visible: harvest.is_correction counts human corrections from the transcript, gate._anomaly makes a correction a reason the unit still earns a retro, and the scorecard counts requirements added after the first verification. Nothing reopens the goal or acceptance criteria; the response is left to the agent's judgement through the retro finding.
gap: No mechanism makes the agent revisit the contract's goal and checks after a correction or a late requirement; only detection and visibility exist (rule 1 advice covers the rest). No test was opened that ties a correction to a changed contract.
fix: Revisiting intent after a correction is judgement; the product can only prompt for it.

how: A change whose risk floor is integration or above is refused until the unit carries invariants, a requirement list, an approach and a risk note (assure.missing, enforced by the contract guard and the gate), and the gate runs the selected checks on the combined tree. Nothing recognises an integration failure as such or assigns ownership of one.
gap: There is no response to an integration failure: no detection, no explicit ownership of the integration, only the up-front contract requirements for integration-risk work.
fix: Owning and responding to integration failure is judgement; code can only require ownership up front.

how: A failed check keeps its scrubbed failure evidence in the record (verify.evidence) and the gate sends the turn back, so a regression cannot be reported as delivered; a recurrence after promotion flags the learning not working and the cycle must revise or revert it; a retro finding is required to close the unit. Blast radius is only a note written before the work (risk.blast_radius) and is never assessed after a regression.
gap: No mechanism assesses the blast radius of a regression, and revert or repair is provided only for sisi's own store changes (cycle revert, sisi rollback), not for the project's regressed change.
fix: Blast radius of a regression is an assessment the agent must make; the product can ask for it.

how: For the authority sisi owns, an unauthorized action is stopped, notified and recorded: watch.refuse_self_approval refuses (exit 2) an agent's shell command that invokes sisi approve, tells the agent to show the owner, and cycle.refuse_attempt writes the attempt with the session id to the approval record; sisi approve itself refuses without the owner's typed word; an untrusted contract's commands are never run and the gate says so once.
gap: Only sisi's own boundaries are covered (approval decisions, untrusted contracts, uncontracted edits). Any other unsafe action by the agent relies on rule 9 in canon/core.md, and nothing contains or detects an unsafe action after it has happened.
fix: Contain and notify on unsafe agent actions beyond sisi's own boundaries.

how: sisi's own consequential operations are checkpointed and recoverable: cycle._transact records the before and after commits and what it changed, restores every file when a cycle fails part-way, and cycle.revert_cycle undoes exactly one cycle; update and install take backups or keep originals. For the project work itself only a written rollback note is demanded of integration-and-above units.
gap: No checkpoint of the project's state is taken before a consequential (data, critical) change; recovery there is a required written rollback note and the project's own git history, neither of which sisi verifies as a working recovery mechanism.
fix: Checkpoint the project state before data or critical changes and verify the rollback works.

how: The end-of-turn gate sends a turn back with the failing checks and, when the send-backs run out, gate._release records the unit as unverified in the results and the contract and tells the agent to report it as unverified; unit.decide_status gives every unit one of five delivery statuses (delivered-with-deferred, deviation, unverified, abandoned), and sisi status lists open and parked units with their age, owed checks and unverified reason.

The constraint is enforced where sisi acts: rule 9 is protected from change by a cycle (canon/protected.json, checked in cycle._plan_rule), secrets are scrubbed from stored records, contracts run only when trusted and policy changes wait for the owner. For the agent's own reasoning and tool use it is a sentence in canon/core.md rule 9 and a SECURITY.md description, which nothing checks.
gap: Across agent reasoning, tools and delegation the requirement rests on written advice (rule 9); the only test that mentions R-16-1 checks SECURITY.md's wording, not behaviour.
fix: Security as a constraint on agent reasoning cannot be checked by code; only advice is possible.

how: The text is the lead-in line "It MUST:" that introduces the items R-16-3 to R-16-11; it places no requirement of its own on the product.
gap: None: a lead-in line only, graded through R-16-3 to R-16-11.

how: Least privilege is enforced for particular inputs: a contract's shell commands run only in a project on the trust list (trust.is_trusted; verify exits 3 elsewhere), a replayed command check runs in an exported copy with an environment of PATH, HOME and LANG only, and a provider key is fetched at probe time and never stored. The agents and tools themselves are not restricted: SECURITY.md states the replayed command still runs as the user with the user's file permissions and is not sandboxed.
gap: There is no general restriction of what the agent, its tools or its subagents may access (files, network, credentials); only contract commands, replayed commands and provider keys are limited.
fix: Restrict agent, tool and subagent file, network and credential access by policy.

how: learning.scrub_secrets redacts keys, tokens and passwords before anything is stored in learnings, findings, owner statements, cycle history and check failure evidence (verify.evidence), and the allowance probe never stores a key. Other stored text is not scrubbed: contract fields in .sisi/contract.json (goal, check commands, risk notes), delegation ledger and worker notes, pause and extension reasons, and the transcript text sisi keeps in its scratch database.
gap: Scrubbing covers learning artifacts and failure evidence only; contract text that can enter the project's source control, the delegation ledger, worker notes and the harvested transcripts and logs are stored as written.
fix: Scrub secrets from contract fields, delegation ledger, worker notes and transcripts before storage.

how: learning.earned_scope and learning.in_scope keep a learning in force only in its origin project until its provenance holds two units in two projects, keep a project-scoped owner statement in its project, deliver only rows sisi's own commands wrote, and learning.learnings_in_scope feeds delivery and the oracle; a cycle cannot widen scope beyond what was earned without the owner (cycle._plan_promote).

sisi treats its own inputs as data: a cycle file written by an agent is untrusted (cycle.validate_doc refuses it whole, and replay_validate ignores the commits, repository and project it names in favour of the learning's own record), and only learnings sisi's own commands wrote are delivered into prompts. Whether the agent treats web pages, issue text and tool output as data is one sentence in canon/core.md rule 9.
gap: Outside sisi's own command inputs there is no mechanism: nothing checks, frames or sanitises retrieved content or tool output before the agent acts on it; that rests on rule 9's written advice.
fix: Treating web pages and tool output as data is the agent's behaviour; sisi cannot check it.

how: External input is validated before sisi acts on it: cycle.validate_doc checks every action of a cycle file and applies nothing unless the file has no problem, a command check must be replayed (fail before the fix, pass after) before it is enforced, and a contract from a clone is not executed until the project is trusted. Results coming back from delegated workers are only asked to be judged (sisi delegate judge) and recorded; no judgement is required before the agent uses a worker's result.
gap: Tool results from subagents are not validated before consequential use: the gate asks for judgements on finished runs but does not refuse, and how the agent checks what a worker returned is not checked by sisi.
fix: Gate consequential use of a worker result on a recorded judgement, refusing it otherwise.

how: The user store is a git repository in which pdata.commit records every change under a lock with a message; each cycle writes cycles/<id>.json with its label, before and after commits, changed files and report lines (cycle._transact); every refused or given approval decision is written to the approval record with time, session id and how (cycle.refuse_attempt); unit records are archived with their policy-version hash and guard refusals.

cycle._transact runs each cycle as one transaction: a failure part-way restores every file it changed and the cycle record keeps what is needed to revert exactly; cycle.revert_cycle undoes one cycle's mechanism files and learning fields only and refuses when a later change touched the same file, leaving later findings and statements in place.

brief.check lists the parts a delegation brief lacks and the delegation hook returns them as "sisi brief advice" (orchestration._before_delegation), never as a refusal; the before-tool approval refusal applies to worker sessions too; a cycle brief carries at most eight learnings. Nothing limits the context a delegation actually carries or the permissions a subagent runs with.
gap: Context minimisation is advice only (a missing brief part is reported, not refused) and no permission is restricted for a subagent, which runs with the host's and the user's permissions.
fix: Refuse delegations carrying context beyond the brief and restrict subagent permissions.

how: cycle._plan_promote marks every consequential change as waiting for the owner (more scope than the learning earned, a command check not seen to fail and then pass, a replaced or disabled rule, a risk pattern that lowers a profile, rule text from a one-project learning) and cycle apply parks it as pending-approval; protected rules are refused outright, even with approval; cmd_approve decides only on the word typed at the controlling terminal, and watch.refuse_self_approval refuses an agent's own attempt by the before-tool hook.
Lead-in line only ('The organization SHOULD:'); the requirements are the items that follow, graded separately.
gap: Nothing to grade in this line.

how: `sisi unit pause "<what it waits for>"` refuses an empty reason, records the wait on the unit, and `sisi status` prints 'waiting for: ...'; the gate offers it as the way to end a turn with work outstanding. Time to first useful result is only measured (sisi/delivery.py); nothing makes the agent tell the user about progress during long work.
gap: A block is recorded, not communicated: nothing checks that a long-running or blocked turn says anything to the user, and the gate's demand for a retro or a pause is bounded.
fix: Communicating progress to the user is the agent's; no code can see the message.

how: sisi's own hooks are silent by default and tested: session start prints nothing when nothing is actionable, the prompt hook injects nothing for a trivial message, the gate passes a session that changed nothing with no message, and a final message naming an internal worker failure is sent back once.
gap: Only what sisi itself emits is controlled; the agent's own narration of routine activity is never read (rule 7 is advice, nothing measures it).
fix: Avoiding noisy narration is a quality of the agent's writing; no code can check it.

how: The end-of-turn gate (sisi/questions.py) sends back a reply that ends by asking a question in prose and directs it to the question dialog with options and a recommendation, or to decide and record the assumption; question dialogs are counted in the scorecard.
gap: Nothing checks that a question is concise or consequential: a dialog with many broad questions passes, and the count is only telemetry.
fix: Whether questions are concise and consequential is judgement; only the count is measurable.

how: `sisi contract waive` records a deviation with its reason, the unit then closes as `deviation` and `sisi unit close` prints that the completion report must say so; lowering the risk floor needs `risk.why`. Assumptions are an optional contract list that no profile requires.
gap: Nothing makes the agent explain an assumption or a deviation to the user: a reminder is printed at close, the assumptions list is never demanded or shown, and no report is read.
fix: Print recorded assumptions and deviations in the close message so they reach the report.

how: Time to first useful result (first allowed stop after a request) is recorded by the delivery recorder and kept as telemetry; handing over an intermediate result is left to the agent by rule 5.
gap: Measured only: no hook, gate or command makes an intermediate result reach the user; it rests on the agent following written advice.
fix: Delivering intermediate results is the agent's choice; no mechanism can force it.

how: The archived unit record holds changed artifacts, every verification result, deferred and never-run checks, limitations and open risks, and `sisi unit close` prints the delivery status. The completion report itself is written by the agent and nothing reads it.
gap: sisi records evidence for a summary but neither produces nor checks the summary, artifacts and limitations the user receives; limitations and open risks are optional fields.
fix: Print a completion summary block from the record at close: artifacts, evidence, limitations.

how: When a worker is unavailable, sisi/fallback.py hands the agent the router's next worker and tells it to fall back without asking or reporting; a question dialog right after is refused once, a turn ending with no fallback is sent back (twice at most), and a final message naming the failed worker is sent back once.
gap: Only the worker-unavailability path is covered, and each refusal is once-only (a second question in the turn is let through); outside it, keeping the user out of worker matters rests on rule 7.
fix: Keeping the user out of worker coordination is judgement beyond the fallback path.

how: Lead-in of the five report items. The unit record stores the material for them (goal and delivery status, approach, verification results, never-run and deferred checks, limitations and risks); the report is the agent's and is not read.
gap: No mechanism makes a completion report contain these items; only the underlying record exists.
fix: Describes what a completion report typically contains; places no testable requirement on the product.

how: The unit record keeps the goal, scope and a delivery status (delivered, delivered-with-deferred, deviation, unverified, abandoned) that `sisi status` prints, and the gate sends back unfinished work with 'Do not report this work as done'. What the report says was delivered is not read.
gap: The outcome is recorded, not reported: nothing checks the user's summary against the unit's delivery status.
fix: Whether the report states the delivered outcome accurately is judgement.

how: The contract's `approach` (chosen, why, at least one alternative) is carried into the unit record and is demanded by the gate for integration and above. Design decisions taken during the work are not recorded unless the agent adds them, and the report is not read.
gap: Below integration no decision record is required, and nothing makes the report mention a decision.
fix: Whether the report mentions important decisions is judgement; ask for it.

how: Every verification result, with its status and failure evidence, is stored in the unit record (`verification`, `final_verification`), and nothing that did not run can be recorded as passed. Whether the report states it is unchecked.
gap: The evidence exists in the record only; no mechanism puts it in, or checks it in, the report.
fix: Whether the report states verification performed is judgement; ask for it.

how: The unit record lists `never_run_mandatory`, `deferred_checks` and `released_unverified`, and telemetry values carry an `unavailable` class; a unit with deferred or human-pending checks closes as delivered-with-deferred. The report's own statement of what is unverified is not read.
gap: Recorded but not reported: nothing checks that the user is told what was not verified.
fix: Whether the report states what was not verified is judgement; ask for it.

how: `open_risks`, `deferred` (what, why, safe_because), `limitations` and deviations are carried in the unit record. All are optional contract fields and the report is not read.
gap: No profile requires risks or follow-up to be recorded, and nothing makes them reach the user.
fix: Whether the report surfaces risks and follow-up is judgement; ask for it.

how: Rule 7 asks for a report in proportion to the change; `sisi rule 7` itself states that nothing reads the words. sisi's own demands are proportional (a trivial change is asked nothing unless the unit shows an anomaly), but that is process, not the report.
gap: Nothing in the code checks or measures the report's length against the size of the change; it rests entirely on the agent following rule 7.
fix: Proportion of the report to the change is judgement; no code measures it sensibly.

how: Several anti-patterns have an enforced mechanism: checks selected by change instead of the full suite, the gate sending back failing or missing mandatory checks, independent evidence that cannot be the author, the fourth identical failing command refused once, a rule from one incident waiting for approval, and self-modification gated by protected rules and owner approval.
gap: I found no detecting mechanism for maximum parallelism (only the parallelism measure), cleverness over clarity, or the value/cost estimate before scope expands; the other refusals are bounded and none measures recurrence.
fix: Detecting clever-over-clear or excess parallelism is judgement; no code can check it.

how: The reconciliation of sisi itself is staged in docs/plan.md, with the dated record in docs/reconciliation/; a test checks that the plan names six stage words.
gap: A plan document and a test of its words: no product code reconciles a project in stages, and the test would not notice the stages being skipped.
fix: Staging a reconciliation is a project process; no product code can enforce it.

how: docs/reconciliation/inventory-base.json freezes an inventory of 41 modules and 47 commands at one commit.
gap: Only modules and commands are inventoried; agents, prompts, tools, workflows, memory stores, evaluators, test infrastructure, policies, metrics and permission boundaries are not identified, and the test checks only two counts of at least 40.
fix: Extend the inventory to agents, prompts, tools, memory, evaluators and policies, with a test.

how: docs/reconciliation/critique.md gives every module and command a verdict (keep, replace, rebuild, simplify, retire) with a short reason.
gap: No component is tied to a requirement id and no evidence is cited per row (a search for 'R-' in the critique finds nothing); the test checks only that each name appears in the document.
fix: Add a requirement id and evidence column per component and test that each is present.

how: The critique sorts defects into flat-out wrong, missing and overbuilt, plus a 'what is good and stays' section.
gap: Ineffective mechanisms, duplicated responsibilities (mentioned once) and conflicting policies (not mentioned) are not classified systematically, and no test guards the classification.
fix: Classifying liabilities is an analytic judgement recorded in the critique document.

how: docs/reconciliation/baseline.json records pre-rebuild counts and hook timings (hook medians, prompt characters, module and test counts).
gap: None of the six asked-for measures (intent fulfilment, correctness evidence, task time, cost, human intervention, rework) is in it, no test reads it, and I did not assess whether sisi/evaluate.py supplies a task-performance baseline.
fix: Measure intent, correctness, time, cost, intervention and rework over representative work as a baseline.

how: Retirement is enforced by tests: dead code in sisi/ fails the suite, and the retired reporters, commands and lesson store are checked to be gone. The keep/rewrite/retire verdict for each module is only a document (docs/reconciliation/critique.md).
gap: No mechanism judges whether a component demonstrably contributes or costs more than its value; that was a one-off judgement written in a document, and nothing checks that useful assets are retained.
fix: Whether a component contributes more than it costs is a judgement; code can only record it.

how: canon/core.md states the objective in order and the rules; canon/protected.json names the non-negotiable rules the cycle refuses to touch; unit.policy_version hashes the rulebook, risk tables, enforced checks and config into every unit record.
gap: The policy-version test varies only a risk table, so nothing fails if the rulebook is dropped from the hash or the objective sentence leaves core.md; the authority model and core definitions are prose, not versioned data.
fix: Add a test that fails when the objective sentence or rulebook is dropped from the policy version.

how: A unit opens with a contract (goal, scope, requirements with kinds, checks that can fail); close_unit archives it with telemetry, changed artifacts and every verification result; the gate asks for a retro and a recorded finding closes the unit.

sisi/learning.py keeps learning records with mechanism type, scope and provenance; sisi/cycle.py validates before promoting, commits each change and revert_cycle restores exactly what a cycle touched.

sisi/evaluate.py captures cases from closed units and compare_for_candidate runs the same cases under the current and a candidate policy, naming regressions and refusing to call a faster but regressing candidate an improvement.

The learning cycle verifies an effect: a promoted learning needs an expected effect and a validation method, a command check must fail before and pass after the fix, and recurrences after promotion flag it. One-bottleneck-at-a-time and no-wholesale-rewrite are not mechanised.
gap: Nothing in the product makes or checks that evolution proceeds one bottleneck at a time or that a rewrite is justified by evidence; I found no record establishing that the rebuild was necessary, only per-module verdicts.
fix: Evolving one bottleneck at a time is a discipline; no code can verify it.

how: The unit record and `sisi status` explain what was done, what it cost, what evidence was produced and what was learned (eight scorecard dimensions, each value classed), and that report is tested. The build order itself is not something the product can show.
gap: Nothing enforces or records that observability came before self-optimization; the cycle is gated on validation, not on the report existing, and the milestone ordering is only a statement in the design.
fix: Build ordering is a design statement the product cannot check.

how: This is the lead-in sentence that introduces the conformance checklist; it places no requirement of its own on the product.
gap: Lead-in only; the capabilities it introduces are graded one by one as R-20.1-1 to R-20.2-6.

how: The objective and its order are written in canon/core.md; canon/protected.json holds the non-negotiable rules, which sisi/cycle.py refuses to replace or disable; unit.policy_version versions the rulebook, risk tables, enforced checks and config per unit.
gap: No test fails if the objective text is removed from core.md, and the policy-version test changes only a risk table, so the rulebook's part of the version is unconfirmed.
fix: Add a test that fails if the objective text is removed from core.md.

how: The contract carries the goal in the person's words and a requirement list with kinds, and for integration and above the gate names each missing piece. Treating intent and ownership as primary is otherwise rule 1, which the agent may follow or not.
gap: Below integration no requirement model is demanded, and nothing checks that the agent pursued the user's actual outcome rather than the literal request; that rests on written advice.
fix: Treating user intent as primary is a quality of thinking; no code can check it.

how: The unit is bound to the main session and the end-of-turn gate judges that session's own edits and sends it back; workers and subagents are exempt from the guards and are never blocked, so the main thread is the one held to delivery.

The contract bounds a unit with goal, scope in/out, requirements and checks that can fail; the before-tool guard (sisi/unitguard.py check) refuses a non-trivial change when the session holds no valid unit, and the gate does the same at end of turn.
verify.record stores every result with status, duration and failure evidence; close_unit archives the unit with its telemetry, changed artifacts, checks, verification results and scorecard.

When checks are green and the unit is open, the gate offers the retro; a recorded, non-generic finding closes the unit and archives it. It is not mandatory: a trivial change is asked nothing, and after three send-backs the gate releases the unit as unverified with no analysis.
gap: The analysis can be skipped: bounded send-backs release the unit without a retro, and units below isolated get no retro unless an anomaly shows.
fix: Bounded send-backs release units without a retro; remove the release path for non-trivial units.

how: Learning records live in the user store with provenance, and scope is earned: a learning from one unit is delivered only in its own project until it is seen in two units in two projects or is an owner statement.

sisi/routing.py picks the cheapest worker that is capable enough for the kind and difficulty from judged records, prices and standings, and the delegation guard refuses a delegation that names no model or the session's own, handing over that pick.

workers.delegations_for_project counts delegations and overlapping pairs for a unit's window and the scorecard's parallelism dimension stores them with worker minutes against wall time. Whether to parallelise rests on rule 6.
gap: No coordination cost is measured (the word appears nowhere in sisi/), and overlap is counted without judging whether it shortened the critical path.
fix: Measure coordination cost and whether overlap shortened the critical path.

how: risk.floor_for_working_tree maps changed paths to a risk floor through canon/risk.json, and the gate demands what that profile needs; verify.run runs a check only when a changed path matches its when_changed and records the skip reason otherwise.

build_scorecard stores time to first result and to completion, tokens and estimated cost, human messages and question dialogs, gate send-backs under retries, and requirements with a passing check, each with a class and unavailable rather than zero.
gap: Rework is only the gate's send-backs (no re-done delegations or edits), outcome quality is only requirements with a passing check plus delivery status, and human corrections are inferred, not measured.
fix: Record human effort and rework as measured values in the scorecard.

how: The fourth identical failing command is refused once with a reason, an unavailable worker is classified and the next worker is handed over (the turn is sent back if no fallback starts), and `sisi route --retry-of` moves to stronger evidence after rejections. There is no time-based stall detection.
gap: Nothing detects a stall over time (no meaningful progress in an interval); the repeat refusal fires once and then the same command is let through, and the send-backs are bounded.
fix: Detect time-based stalls with no meaningful progress and change strategy.

how: learning.delivery_text selects the learnings in scope for the request and prompt.build_context adds them to what the session is given, so a later session in scope receives them without asking.

unit.policy_version hashes the rulebook, both risk tables, the enforced checks and the gate/verify config into a version stored on every closed unit and used as a trend segment; rollback is cycle.revert_cycle (sisi cycle revert, restores the files and records one cycle changed) and release.cmd_rollback (sisi rollback, returns to the previous release).

Closing a unit stores a benchmark case from the real work (evaluate.capture_case) and harvested tasks become cases (taskset.to_benchmark_case); a cycle can add a case for a learning (the benchmark action).
gap: The failure-mode half is untested: the cycle's benchmark action (sisi/cycle.py:587) is only exercised by a path-escape refusal test, and no test shows a promoted case landing in the suite.
fix: Add a test that a promoted failure-mode case lands in the benchmark suite.

how: Cases carry a dev/holdout/counterexample split, select_cases refuses held-out cases for tuning or shadow runs, and compare_for_candidate runs a dev sample plus every counterexample under a candidate policy; compare_versions refuses to call a regressing candidate an improvement.
gap: Nothing makes a policy change be tested: compare_for_candidate is called only from the eval command line (sisi/evaluate.py:1522), so a promoted or approved policy is never blocked for lacking a comparison, and the holdout split is never run by an automatic path.
fix: Require holdout and counterexample comparison before approving any policy change.

how: evaluate.judge_result stores an outside judge's verdict with judged_by and refuses a judge from the same maker as the worker, so a self-assessment is never recorded as independent.
