gap: Judging is only started by the eval command (the sole caller is sisi/evaluate.py:1536); no gate, cycle or close requires an independent judgement, so self-scored results are simply left unjudged rather than refused.
fix: Require an independent judgement before a promotion is accepted, not only when eval is run.

how: A learning can name mechanism verification, and a cycle promotes a learning into an enforced command check or contract requirement, the command check being replayed to fail before and pass after the fix.
gap: The cycle's mechanism kinds are contract-requirement, command-check, library, rule-add, rule-replace, risk, routing and benchmark only; the retro's verification mechanism type has no action of its own, and nothing measures whether assurance gets stronger over time.
fix: Whether verification infrastructure improves over time is judgement, not a code check.

how: compare_versions sets median and p95 minutes and cost beside pass rate and returns 'not an improvement' when a case that passed now fails; sisi status prints time trends by project, risk profile, model and policy version.
gap: The comparison has no user-acceptance counter-metric (only pass rate), cost is absent from the status trends, and no reduction is demonstrated: both tools must be run by hand on enough cases.
fix: Demonstrating latency and cost reduction needs real runs; no code can show it.

how: The scorecard counts requirements added after the first verification (surprise) and human corrections (inferred) for each unit.
gap: Surprise is not among the trend metrics, so no change over time is shown; human corrections are inferred from the transcript; and nothing demonstrates improvement in requirement inference.
fix: Add requirements-added-after-verification to the trend metrics in sisi status.

how: add_recurrence counts recurrences after promotion and flags a learning after two; learning_report prints units since, recurrences, a verdict and a realization rate only when five promoted learnings have five relevant units; a cycle that leaves a flagged learning unacted is refused.
gap: The effect is measured only as absence of a resembling finding; the expected effect recorded at promotion is stored and printed (sisi/cycle.py:304) but never measured, and nothing is demonstrated until the thresholds are met.
fix: Measure the expected effect recorded at promotion, not only absence of recurrence.

how: learning_report says no improvement is claimed from counts and prints 'too few' instead of a rate; trends print 'too few' under five units and no single score; a comparison that regresses is verdicted 'not an improvement'.
gap: Compliance rests on the wording of three reporters; no code joins learning counts to outcomes, and I found no test that would fail if another report (retro, lessons, workers, session start) claimed improvement from counts.
fix: Add a test that fails if any report claims improvement from counts alone.

how: docs/design.md records the choices sisi made (where things live, risk profiles, record fields, enforcement) with SPEC section numbers in brackets.
gap: Documentation only: links are to section numbers, not to requirement ids, none of the ten listed decisions is called an implementation decision or traced one by one, and no test would fail if the links were removed.
fix: Link design decisions to requirement ids and test that each link resolves.

how: canon/protected.json names five non-negotiable rules a cycle must never replace or disable, rule changes that reach every project are held for the owner's decision, and SPEC.md is pinned by hash in tests/test_spec.py.
gap: The protected list names rule ids, not the objective statement in the rulebook's opening section; I found no check that a rule-add, a rule-replace or an owner statement leaves that statement unchanged, so non-redefinition rests on the owner reading what he approves.
fix: Protect the objective statement in the rulebook so no rule-add or replace can change it.

how: sisi status groups closed units by project, risk profile, model and policy version and reports median and p95 only for segments of five or more units.
gap: It segments comparable work but judges nothing: no output says whether the organization is succeeding, and increasing difficulty is not modelled beyond the risk profile.
fix: Whether the organization is succeeding is a judgement no output can make.

how: The contract guard refuses a non-trivial build until the unit carries a requirement list, and the scorecard records requirements total, those with a passing check, surprise and human corrections.
gap: sisi forces a requirement list and measures it, but the list is the agent's own words: nothing checks that the requirements match the user's actual intent, and no improvement over time is shown.
fix: Whether requirements match the user's intent is judgement; the owner must confirm.

how: A requirement's kind can be implied or anticipated and its decision now, architect, defer or ignore, with the contract also holding scope in and out and deferred items.
gap: The fields exist but are filled in by the agent; I found no check that implied needs were looked for, and prompting and scope waste are only partly counted (question dialogs), with no trend.
fix: Anticipating implied needs is judgement; the product can only record what was considered.

how: assure.missing and the gate require, by risk profile, a contract, non-vacuous checks with covers, invariants, a risk note and independent evidence; a result that did not run is never reported as passed.
gap: The gate checks that evidence is present, able to fail and honestly labelled; it does not judge whether a check is strong or relevant enough for its claim, which is left to the agent's prose in covers.
fix: Whether a check is strong enough for its claim is judgement left to the agent.

how: The scorecard records time to first useful result and to validated completion, and sisi status prints their median and p95 per segment.
gap: Measured and trended only: no mechanism or verdict shows delivery getting faster, and the time values come from telemetry that may be unavailable.
fix: Derive a trend verdict showing delivery getting faster across comparable units.

how: The router picks the cheapest capable worker, the before-tool hook refuses direct work past a budget and delegations that name no model or the session's own, and the scorecard records tokens and estimated cost per unit.
gap: Allocation is enforced, but cost per accepted and verified change is not computed or trended (the status trends carry tokens, not cost), and no reduction is demonstrated.
fix: Compute and trend cost per accepted and verified change across units.

how: The scorecard counts human messages, question dialogs and inferred corrections and trends corrections; the hooks keep the agent inside authorization (contract guard, protected rules, approve needing a typed word).
gap: Supervision burden is counted, not reduced by any mechanism, corrections are inferred, and a fall in corrections is never set against authorization breaches to show one without the other.
fix: Reducing supervision burden is an outcome of the work; code can only count it.

how: The scorecard records files and lines changed, tests changed with code and public surface touched, and the gate requires invariants for what exists from the integration profile up.
gap: Lifecycle quality is measured per unit and is not among the trend metrics; nothing checks that quality or evolvability improves.
fix: Whether long-term quality improves is judgement; code can only measure size and surface.

how: At the end of a green turn the gate offers the retro or a pause, a retro needs at least one concrete finding and closes the unit, and the cycle validates a command check by replay before promoting it.
gap: Not every engagement: a trivial change is asked nothing and a pause ends the turn with no finding; a finding may be recorded or dropped; and only command checks are validated, the other mechanism kinds take effect unvalidated.
fix: Trivial units and pauses exempt from findings by design; remove the exemption to close it.

how: Learnings in scope are delivered with each prompt, a recurrence after promotion counts against the learning, two flag it, and a cycle that does not revise or revert a flagged learning is refused.
gap: sisi reminds and flags but cannot make the organization avoid a known failure; sustained benefit is inferred from absence of recurrence of a resembling finding, not from the expected effect, and no benefit is demonstrated.
fix: Sustained benefit and avoided failures are judgement; absence of recurrence is only a proxy.
